#1603. Wrexham's Hollywood owners Ryan Reynolds and Rob McElhenney jet in to watch clash with Wolves after surprise exit of club's CEO - and catch up with poppy-protest footballer James McClean in the stands

By BEN WILLCOCKS, ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR

Published: 08:39 EST, 7 November 2026 | Updated: 10:40 EST, 7 November 2026

Wrexham's celebrity owners Ryan Reynolds and Rob McElhenney have travelled to watch their side's Championship clash with Wolves less than a day after announcing chief executive Michael Williamson's surprise departure.

Reynolds and McElhenney announced in a joint statement on Friday that Williamson was leaving the club after two years at the Racecourse Ground, with club director Shaun Harvey set to take the reins as acting CEO while they seek a successor.

'We thank Michael Williamson for his two years at Wrexham and for his work taking the club from League 1 to the Championship,' the Hollywood actors' statement read.

'Since our takeover five years ago, Wrexham have had historic success on the pitch and won hearts all over the globe.

'We remain focused on our most important task: to make the Wrexham community proud.

'Shaun Harvey has been an integral part of this journey from the beginning, and we know Shaun will give every support to (manager) Phil Parkinson and the lads on the pitch while keeping the broader Wrexham community roaring us on.'

Rob McElhenney and Ryan Reynolds pictured watching Wrexham take on Wolves on Saturday

The American actor takes photos with supporters as he arrives at the Racecourse Ground

Williamson arrived at Wrexham in 2024 and oversaw a period that saw the club win promotion from League One to the Championship and consolidate themselves in the second tier, narrowly missing out on the playoffs with a seventh-place finish.

Wrexham's form this campaign has been less fruitful, with just four wins so far leaving Parkinson's side in 17th place heading into Saturday's clash with Wolves.

After arriving and meeting fans outside the stadium, Reynolds and McElhenney took their place in the Racecourse Ground stands hoping to watch their Wrexham side earn back-to-back wins for the first time this season.

Wolves, who were relegated from the Premier League last season, took the lead in the 25th minute before Wrexham's Lewis O'Brien equalised moments later, to the delight of the celebrity owners.

As the matched ebbed and flowed, both sides fought hard for a winning goal but ended up settling for a share of the spoils, the 1-1 draw moving Wrexham to 15th and Wolves to third in the Championship.

After the match, Parkinson backed Harvey to adapt seamlessly to his new temporary CEO role, saying:  'Ryan spoke to me yesterday morning to let me know the news. I had a brief chat with Shaun this morning; he has been an important figure. He understands everything about the club.'

While watching the 1-1 draw, Reynolds was pictured chatting to former Wrexham star James McClean, who left the Racecourse Ground to join his hometown team Derry City in January.

McClean's appearance at Wrexham is particularly poignant on Remembrance Weekend, given the controversy he courted throughout his career by refusing to wear football shirts featuring a poppy.

Reynolds pictured chatting to former Wrexham footballer James McClean in the stands

Wrexham players, displaying poppies, observe a minute of silence on Remembrance weekend

Clubs across English football will observe a period of silence before matches this weekend, with players also wearing poppy-adorned shirts to honour those who lost their lives in conflict.

McClean's objection to wearing a poppy is rooted in his upbringing in Derry, having grown up on the Creggan estate, where six of the 13 civilians shot dead by British soldiers on Bloody Sunday in 1972 were from.

#1602. Liverpool transfer news: Reds 'express interest' in £21m Milos Kerkez upgrade ahead of January window

By Lewis Blain | 10 Nov 2026 07:59

Liverpool have joined the race to sign Juventus defender Andrea Cambiaso ahead of the January transfer window.

The Italian international is attracting interest from several European clubs, with Barcelona and Manchester United also monitoring his situation.

A potential deal could offer Andoni Iraola an opportunity to strengthen his defensive options with a versatile addition.

According to reports in Italy, Liverpool have 'expressed interest' in Cambiaso as a potential January target, with the left-back valued at around €25m (£21m).

Barcelona and United are also among the clubs taking a look at the 26-year-old, whose ability to operate on either flank makes him an attractive option for several tactical systems.

United are understood to be assessing reinforcements on the left side of their defence, while the Catalan giants are considering whether out-of-favour Alejandro Balde could be involved in a possible swap deal.

However, the Serie A outfit could prove difficult to negotiate with, particularly given Cambiaso's versatility and importance to their squad.

Both full-back positions have been problematic for Iraola since he arrived from AFC Bournemouth in the summer, and Cambiaso could offer some respite, particularly on the left flank.

His numbers this season suggest he could offer the Reds some advantages over current option Milos Kerkez, particularly in possession and when contributing to attacks.

Cambiaso has averaged 88.5% successful passes compared with Kerkez's 78.8%. The Juventus defender also leads for assists (0.43 to 0.00 per 90), tackles (3.03 to 1.64 per 90) and accurate crosses (1.30 to 0.66 per 90).

Kerkez, however, comes out ahead in duels won, averaging 5.02 per 90 compared with Cambiaso's 4.33, while he also draws more fouls (1.75 to 1.30).

There is an important caveat, as Cambiaso has played just 208 minutes across seven Serie A appearances, compared with Kerkez's 824 minutes across ten Premier League outings. The sample sizes are therefore very different, making direct conclusions difficult.

Cambiaso has the statistical profile to offer Liverpool greater quality in possession and attacking output, while his ability to be able to play right-back also appeals.

At around £21m, he could be an attractive potential upgrade and provide valuable competition for Kerkez, as well as cover on the opposite flank.

#1601. Celik and Nico Gonzalez injuries add to Juventus absences before Lecce

Juventus will travel to Lecce without Zeki Celik and Nico Gonzalez after both players picked up muscle injuries in Thursday’s 2-2 Europa League draw with Rennes, adding two more names to an already long absence list for Luciano Spalletti.

The club confirmed the diagnoses in an official medical update on Friday, October 23. Both players had felt muscle discomfort after the Rennes match and went for tests at J|medical that morning.

According to the club, Celik has a low-grade injury to the biceps femoris in his left leg, while Nico Gonzalez has a low-grade injury to the soleus muscle in his right calf. Juventus said both players have already started their rehabilitation programmes, but the statement did not give a return date for either of them.

Medical Update | Çelik and Nico González’s conditions

🗞️ https://t.co/BHwNzeidQ7 pic.twitter.com/YUXRK97IwL

— JuventusFC 🇬🇧🇺🇸 (@juventusfcen) October 23, 2026

The timing is frustrating for Celik in particular. The Turkish full-back opened the scoring against Rennes in the fifth minute, converting a pass from Nick Woltemade, before being taken off at half-time. You can read how the rest of that night unfolded in our report on the Rennes draw.

Juventus have not put a timeframe on either recovery, so any estimate comes from the Italian press. Virgilio Sport reports that both players are expected to be out for around 20 days and should only return after the November international break, with the home game against Venezia on November 22 named as the first realistic target.

If that estimate holds, the pair would miss the trip to Lecce, the meeting with Genoa, the home game against Napoli, the Europa League visit to AZ Alkmaar and the match with Fiorentina. That is a demanding run to face with a thinner squad, and it comes at a point when Juventus are trying to recover from the 3-0 home defeat by Lazio.

Celik and Nico Gonzalez join Kenan Yildiz, Manuel Locatelli, Khéphren Thuram and Francisco Conceicao on the sidelines, according to Tuttosport. Conceicao is already in rehabilitation after the shoulder problem he picked up against Lazio, as covered in our Francisco Conceicao injury update.

Tuttosport’s expected line-up has Spalletti sticking with a 3-5-2, with Pierre Kalulu and Andrea Cambiaso on the flanks and Woltemade partnering Randal Kolo Muani in attack. The match at the Via del Mare kicks off at 18:00 Italian time on Sunday, October 25, with Maresca as referee.

Supporters will also have to wait until matchday to hear from the coach. Tuttosport reports that Spalletti, in agreement with the club, will not hold his usual press conference on the eve of the Lecce game. The paper links the decision to the packed schedule after the Europa League fixture, and Virgilio Sport notes that Spalletti has taken the same approach before during congested spells, with no controversy behind the choice.

The squeeze on the squad is now the bigger story. With two more first-team players ruled out and the injury list still growing, Spalletti will need his remaining options to carry the load through a busy stretch of Serie A and European fixtures before the international break.

Sources: Juventus FC, Tuttosport, Virgilio Sport

Sergio Lattanzi has followed Juventus since the days of the Trap, when Serie A felt like the centre of the football world and the Bianconeri were its undisputed rulers. Born and raised in Turin, he developed an early obsession with the tactical patterns that made Juventus so difficult to beat, and that curiosity never left him. He watches matches with a notepad nearby and a tendency to rewind passages of play more times than anyone around him considers reasonable.

#1599. Chelsea transfer news: Defender attracts seven suitors, including Manchester City and Liverpool

By Axel Clody | 10 Nov 2026 08:43

A defender is ready to leave Chelsea in the January transfer window and Chelsea will not stand in his way. Seven suitors have already been identified.

Having arrived at Chelsea in the summer of 2023 from Lyon for £25.5m (€30m), Malo Gusto has played more than 30 matches in each of his three seasons. The 23-year-old had managed to gain importance and even establish himself as a starter last season at right-back, with 49 appearances, including 36 starts.

It was a fine campaign, which prompted Paris Saint-Germain to test the waters for the France international, while Manchester City were also interested in his profile. However, Chelsea set a prohibitive price of £74m for the former Lyon player. It is a decision the London club’s hierarchy may now regret.

Indeed, with the arrival of Xabi Alonso as Chelsea manager, Gusto has lost his place in the starting XI.

He has made ten appearances, but has started only three times in the Premier League. His situation has been complicated by the summer signing of Marco Palestra and the use of young Josh Acheampong in that position, while Reece James is still at the club.

According to TeamTalk, the Frenchman, who has just been called up for this international break by Zinedine Zidane, wants to leave to rediscover regular playing time. For their part, Chelsea are open to a departure for their protege and would reportedly be prepared to listen to offers.

In that respect, the price Chelsea ask will need to be significantly lower than the one demanded this summer, unless a loan departure is preferred. No further details have emerged on the matter.

Nevertheless, the British outlet insists that Manchester City are still interested in Gusto, but it remains to be seen whether they will be able to sign players this winter, with financial sanctions hanging over the club.

In the Premier League, Liverpool and Tottenham are two other potential destinations for the Chelsea player.

Liverpool, who already enquired about his situation in the summer, are open to signing a specialist right-back in 2027, with Ronald Araujo currently filling in at that position.

Abroad, TeamTalk does not mention the presence of PSG in the race, but says that Atletico Madrid, AC Milan, Como and RB Leipzig have also shown an interest in Gusto. It remains to be seen whether any of these seven suitors will make a move this winter and what form a potential deal could take.

#1598. Lecce vs Juventus: in-form hosts await Spalletti’s stretched side at the Via del Mare

Juventus face Lecce at the Stadio Via del Mare this evening, and the fixture arrives at an awkward moment for Luciano Spalletti. His side are still looking for a first win since the 3-0 home defeat by Lazio, while Di Francesco’s Lecce come into Matchday 8 on the back of their most convincing result of the season.

Kick-off is at 18:00 Italian time, which is 17:00 in the UK and Ireland.

Lecce travelled to Udinese last weekend and came away with a 3-0 victory. According to Flashscore, Kialonda Gaspar headed in the opener from a Gallo corner in the 14th minute, and N’Dri doubled the lead in the 25th minute after Tiago Gabriel had gone up for a header. Siebert added the third four minutes from time after a ball was won from Ekkelenkamp.

It was Lecce’s first win in Udine for six years and handed Udinese a fifth straight league defeat. Fatah also hit the crossbar, so the margin could have been even wider. For a side that has spent much of its recent history fighting at the wrong end of the table, it was a timely lift before the visit of Juventus.

The picture is very different in Turin. The heavy home loss to Lazio was followed by a 2-2 draw with Rennes in the Europa League, and the injury list has kept growing. Zeki Celik and Nico Gonzalez are the latest names to drop out, as covered in our Celik and Nico Gonzalez injury update, and Spalletti chose not to give a pre-match press conference on Saturday.

The Lazio defeat in Turin left Juventus well short of the Serie A leaders, so Sunday is about more than one result. Three points in Puglia would ease some of the pressure that has built up over the past week.

Juventus do not have to look far back for a good memory of this trip. The club’s own retrospective recalls the Matchday 36 meeting at the Via del Mare in May 2026, when Dusan Vlahovic scored after just 12 seconds. Kenan Yildiz started the move, Teun Koopmeiners was involved in the build-up and Andrea Cambiaso delivered the ball for Vlahovic to finish into the roof of the net.

That game stayed lively. Michele Di Gregorio had to make a fine save at the other end, Francisco Conceicao struck the crossbar and Vlahovic had another good chance, all inside the first six minutes. Pierre Kalulu thought he had added a second with around half an hour to play, but VAR ruled it out for a marginal Vlahovic offside in the build-up. The early goal proved enough for the win.

Several of the players involved that day, including Yildiz and Conceicao, are now injured, which shows how much Spalletti’s options have changed since May.

Tuttosport reports that Maresca will referee the match. In Italy it is live on DAZN and Sky. In the United Kingdom the game is shown on DAZN UK and Prime Video UK, in Ireland on DAZN, and in the United States on Paramount+, fuboTV and Peacock, according to the club’s broadcast guide.

Published: 10:59 EST, 7 November 2026 | Updated: 11:04 EST, 7 November 2026

Roberto De Zerbi questioned Tottenham’s character after his side’s second-half surrender saw them slip to defeat at Leeds.

#1596. England vs Croatia - prediction, team news, lineups

By Ben Knapton | 10 Nov 2026 09:26, Last updated: 10 Nov 2026 09:34

One point away from progressing to the UEFA Nations League quarter-finals, England's penultimate League A Group 3 fixture sees Croatia rock up to Wembley on Thursday evening.

Thomas Tuchel has masterminded three straight triumphs in the tournament, whereas his opposite number Slaven Bilic has overseen three consecutive defeats, including the infamous 7-0 slaughter at the hands of the Three Lions.

Hoisting the Nations League trophy aloft would not quite quell the excruciating pain of England's World Cup 2026 semi-final exit - which Tuchel and his squad have supposedly now held frank discussions about - but the Three Lions are now almost certain to end their eight-year exile from the latter stages.

Since placing third in the inaugural 2018-19 edition, England have been limited to group-stage appearances in the Nations League - including a brief stint in the second tier in 2024-25 - but one draw from their final two games against Croatia and Spain will suffice for a spot in the last eight.

A narrow 3-2 reverse to the world champions first up preceded back-to-back wins over the Czech Republic and the crushing of Croatia for England, who sit three points behind leaders Spain and six points better off than Bilic's men, while also possessing the best goal difference in the entirety of the Nations League (+11).

Tuchel's charges have racked up 14 goals from their four games - also the most across all four tiers - while letting in just three at the other end, keeping three straight clean sheets since shipping a trio to Spain in September.

Furthermore, England have only ever failed to score in one Nations League game at Wembley - their 1-0 defeat to Denmark in 2020 - since when they have amassed 20 goals in seven matches under the arch.

Boasting a marginally superior pedigree to England in the Nations League, having finished as runners-up to Spain in the 2022-23 edition, Croatia are now at severe risk of losing their perpetual League A status.

While England started with a loss and have now won three on the spin, the Chequered Ones commenced proceedings by beating the Czech Republic but have since taken zero points from the last nine on offer, going down twice to Spain and once to the Three Lions.

In order to pip England to second place now, Croatia must not only win both of their remaining games and hope Tuchel's men lose both of theirs, but also beat the Three Lions by at least seven goals; head-to-head results take precedence over regular goal difference in a tie-breaker scenario.

The odds of such an extraordinary turn of events are slim to none, and Croatia's current third-placed ranking could lead to a potential promotion/relegation playoff, depending on how they rank among other third-placed sides in League A.

Visiting fans need no reminding of last month's catastrophic 7-0 hammering at the hands of England, their biggest defeat on record in a senior men's international, and the Three Lions have now strung together a four-game winning streak against their lowly foes.

Returning to his homeland with the Ballon d'Or trophy glistening on his mantelpiece, England skipper Harry Kane is now poised to make even more history, as the Bayern Munich marksman will break Peter Shilton's all-time caps record if he makes his 126th Three Lions appearance on Thursday.

Kane will line up in a Three Lions side still missing Chelsea playmaker Cole Palmer - snubbed once again by Tuchel after withdrawing from the September/October selection - and Manchester City's Marc Guehi, absent through injury.

Josh King and Jobe Bellingham represent England's only two uncapped outfield players in the November selection, but Tuchel should hold off on giving either man his full debut, as the German prioritises sealing quarter-final qualification before the weekend's showdown with Spain.

Myles Lewis-Skelly, meanwhile, is banned, having picked up two yellow cards in League A so far.

Speaking of suspensions, Croatia veteran Ivan Perisic will also miss Thursday's reunion with the Three Lions, having been sent off for two bookable offences in their 2-1 loss to Spain last time out.

To make matters worse, Bilic has lost five players due to injury since making his selection; defenders Josip Sutalo and Martin Pongracic, attackers Andrej Kramaric and Franjo Ivanovic, and midfielder Kristijan Jakic.

However, the evergreen Luka Modric retains the armband for the visitors and is poised to win his 207th cap for his country at the age of 41.

Pickford; Alexander-Arnold, Konsa, Branthwaite, Hall; Rice, Anderson; Rogers, Bellingham, Gordon; Kane

Livakovic; Stanisic, Vuskovic, Caleta-Car, Gvardiol; Modric, Kovacic; Vlasic, Mario Pasalic, Baturina; Budimir

The days of Croatia giving England a rough ride are over, and the Chequered Ones head to Wembley having kept just one clean sheet in their last 14 fixtures across all competitions.

A repeat of October's sensational seven-goal triumph is surely off the cards regardless, but we still have total faith in Tuchel's men to seal their quarter-final spot in style.

AC Milan ensured they will go into the international break in good spirits as they beat Genoa 2-1 away from home on Sunday.

Milan led by two goals inside 20 minutes after Alphadjo Cisse slotted in a cut-back from Adrien Rabiot to get his eighth of the campaign, before Christian Pulisic buried a square pass from Gonçalo Ramos after a stray pass inside the box.

Ellertsson scored with a strike from distance inside the final few minutes to make it a nervy finale, but Milan did ultimately manage to hang on for what was an important three points that moves them back into the top four.

#1594. Douglas Luiz finally opens his Juventus account as Spalletti hails display at Lecce

Douglas Luiz has finally scored for Juventus. The Brazilian midfielder found the net in Sunday’s 2-0 win at Lecce, more than two years after his €50m move from Aston Villa, and he also set up the opening goal for Weston McKennie.

It was a night that changed the conversation around a player who has spent much of his time in Turin under scrutiny. Luciano Spalletti was quick to single him out afterwards, and the club’s own numbers show just how rare an evening like this has been for him.

According to the standout stats published by Juventus on Monday, this was the first time Douglas Luiz had both scored and assisted in the same match in Europe’s top five leagues. Before Sunday he had made 261 appearances in those competitions without managing it.

The club also points out that he now has two goal involvements from eight Serie A appearances this season, one goal and one assist. In the 2024/25 campaign he played 19 league games for Juventus and failed to register either.

Both contributions came before the break. His free kick was dinked over the Lecce defence for McKennie to break the offside line and slide in on 29 minutes. Twelve minutes later, Federico Gatti laid the ball off and Douglas Luiz hit it first time from outside the box into the far corner.

Douglas Luiz’s first goal in Bianconero! ⚪⚫ pic.twitter.com/g2vTIhUEnF

JuventusFC 🇬🇧🇺🇸 (@juventusfcen) October 25, 2026

The midfielder did not dwell on the personal milestone. In comments shared by the club’s press room after the game, he put the result first.

“The most important thing today was to win. I’m really happy with the result because we’ve worked so hard, and I’m delighted for the team. This victory also gives us the confidence we need,” he said.

He was also honest about the second half, when Lecce pushed Juventus back. “We played well in the first half, but I think we could definitely have done better in the second. We need to improve and perform well for the full 90 minutes.”

Speaking to DAZN, he added that the set piece routine involving Teun Koopmeiners is something the squad practises a lot, and that the players were pleased for their coach after a difficult week, as Tuttosport reported.

Spalletti had already explained after the 3-0 defeat by Lazio that he wanted changes, as covered in our piece on the changes Spalletti identified. Since then Juventus have moved to a three-man midfield, and Douglas Luiz has been one of the beneficiaries.

Speaking to Sky Sport Italia, the coach was full of praise for the Brazilian. “He had a great game today, he fought and ran, he battled on all sides and he helped clean up certain situations when we needed him to,” Spalletti said, in quotes reported by Football Italia.

He came off after 82 minutes, replaced by Sarr, having done the bulk of the work in a side that had only 17 outfield players available. With Manuel Locatelli and Khéphren Thuram among the absentees listed in our latest injury update, Spalletti needs exactly this kind of reliability from his remaining midfielders.

One good night does not settle a debate that has followed Douglas Luiz since his arrival. What it does give him is a platform. If he can keep producing this level of energy and quality in a system that suits him, the midfielder who struggled to make an impact in his first season may yet become an important figure for Spalletti this term.

Sources: Juventus FC, Football Italia, Tuttosport

Born and raised in Turin, he developed an early obsession with the tactical patterns that made Juventus so difficult to beat, and that curiosity never left him. He watches matches with a notepad nearby and a tendency to rewind passages of play more times than anyone around him considers reasonable.

#1592. Allegri banned for Juventus reunion as Napoli lodge appeal

Massimiliano Allegri will not be on the Napoli bench when his side visit the Allianz Stadium on Sunday night. Serie A’s sporting judge has suspended the former Juventus coach for two matches following his dismissal against Roma, although Napoli have confirmed they will challenge the decision.

The ban means one of the most talked about reunions of the autumn could take place without its main character in the dugout, unless the appeal goes Napoli’s way before the weekend.

Allegri was sent off late in Saturday’s 3-3 draw with Roma at the Maradona, reacting furiously after Leonardo Balerdi struck a late equaliser for the visitors. As Football Italia reported, he removed his jacket and walked away before returning and having to be held back by his own staff.

The judge’s ruling, published on Monday and detailed by Sky Sport Italia, goes further than the touchline incident. Allegri was punished for an insulting remark aimed at the match officials in the 90th minute, a seriously disrespectful comment directed at them in the dressing room area afterwards, and aggressive behaviour towards an executive of the opposing club. The first two were noted by the fourth official and the referee, the last by staff working for the federal prosecutor.

On top of the suspension, the 59-year-old has been fined €10,000.

The two games Allegri is set to miss are both away from home. Napoli travel to Monza in the midweek round on Wednesday 28 October, before heading to Turin to face Juventus on Sunday 1 November, with both matches kicking off at 20:45 local time.

If the ban stands, his first game back on the bench would be the home fixture against Lazio on Sunday 8 November.

Official SSC Napoli (@sscnapoli) October 26, 2026

Napoli moved quickly. In a short club statement on Monday afternoon, the Partenopei said that, having requested access to the official documents, they would lodge an appeal against the two match suspension handed to their coach.

Sky Sport Italia notes that a successful appeal would open the door for Allegri to take his place on the bench in Turin. Italian reports suggest the case should be heard before the end of the week, so the picture ought to be clear before Sunday.

For Juventus supporters, any meeting with Allegri carries extra weight. He led the club across two spells, the second of which ended in May 2024, and he remains one of the most successful coaches in its history.

Luciano Spalletti’s side head into the week in a better mood after ending a 35 day wait for a league win with the 2-0 victory at Lecce, which lifted them to seventh on 14 points. Douglas Luiz was among the scorers that night, as covered in our report on his first goal for the club.

Whether or not Allegri is in the dugout, Napoli will arrive as a dangerous opponent. You can follow every twist in his relationship with the Bianconeri on our Massimiliano Allegri page.

#1591. GdS: Week-long breaks and lighter sessions – Amorim bringing ‘international culture’ to Milanello

Ruben Amorim’s decisions when it comes to training have once again come under the microscope after the win over Genoa.

La Gazzetta dello Sport report that Amorim’s closing message to the players after the victory at the Marassi was music to their ears: ‘See you next Monday’. Until early next week, Milanello will remain closed, leaving the players free to recover from the early season grind.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Who knows if things might have been different had the trip to Genoa had gone differently, but the victory that put Milan back in the Champions League spot is worth the reward of a full seven days off. in the eyes of the coach.

An oddity: Serie A teams usually have a break during the international break, but not this long. It’s also worth noting that Milan’s 13 internationals are currently busy traveling around Europe and the world, while the injured players will also continue to follow their respective recovery programs.

As a reminder, Amorim gave those who were not called up by their national teams eight days off for the last international break. However, if must be remembered that it was an extended three-week one, so there was more runway before games resumed.

The extended break is not the first change introduced by Amorim and his staff. For example, the Tuesday rest granted to the team on the eve of the European trip to Bournemouth. The Rossoneri returned to the pitch on Wednesday, the same day they left for England.

This is an unusual approach compared to the traditional post-match rest schedule or a maximum of three or four days of rest during league breaks. Amorim’s training methods are also new, exemplifying the ‘international culture’ the coach seeks to instil at Milanello.

On the pitch, the sessions are never too hard or tiring. The Portuguese coach himself explained the thinking behind it, emphasising that among the many matches scheduled, the tactics and movements were essentially practiced in-game due to the limited time available between matches.

The concept of over-working players in training amidst a demanding fixture list was thought to be the cause of the many Milan injuries suffered during similar periods. Amorim has sought to rectify it, but then the list of absences for the Genoa game was long, so it all remains a work in progress.

But Sávio stepped off the substitutes’ bench to take the limelight with a late goal just a few days after completing his expensive switch from Manchester City, and head coach Roberto De Zerbi is demanding many more to come.

Having watched some of Tottenham’s signings fall to a 3-0 Premier League defeat by Brentford a few days earlier, Sávio’s late impact was the perfect lift for the Spurs supporters.

The club have committed to spending almost £400m this summer, leading to debate by outsiders over whether it will prove to be money well spent and huge waves of excitement within the fanbase.

A deal that could be worth as much as £85m, if add-ons are achieved, for Sávio certainly raised some eyebrows, but the Brazilian provided the perfect response by scoring just 11 minutes into his debut as a late substitute.

In the 82nd minute, Sávio cut in from the flank and scored with a shot past Charlton goalkeeper Tiernan Brooks. He and the Spurs crowd thought he had a second a few minutes later, but his shot hit Ben Davies on its way into the net and the defender was credited with the goal.

Having sung for Moore earlier in the game, the Spurs fans wasted no time in trying out their new song for Sávio, inspired by the Spandau Ballet hit Gold.

Moore has been expected to move to Cologne on loan, but provided a reminder of his talent by opening the scoring in the first half with only his second goal for the club.

What a hit from Mikey Moore! ⚪ pic.twitter.com/OgSM4qhiqs

“We have to understand the best solution,” De Zerbi said. “I would like to keep him. He’s young but a good player, but we can’t make the wrong decision. He needs to play, he needs to get games inside him.”

Cutting in from the right, where Sávio is primed to play, Moore surged past his marker and shot from just inside the box. Brooks should have stopped it, but the ball flew past him and into the net.

Three minutes after Moore’s opener, Dominic Solanke scored his first goal since March to offer a reminder of what he can still give De Zerbi, who is poised to welcome Omar Marmoush to Tottenham.

Buoyed by his first-half goal, Moore skipped his way around a couple of tackles at the start of the second period but his low cross was cut out. The Spurs fans responded by singing “he’s one of our own.”

Substitute Kevin Danso netted with his first touch from a header, before Sávio was introduced to steal the show, despite a late consolation goal from Charlton’s Lloyd Jones.

Kevin Danso scores with his first touch since coming on! ⚪ pic.twitter.com/oqUU7wjoJW

The victory set up a tough third-round trip to Anfield to face Liverpool for Tottenham, but De Zerbi said: “It’s a great game. If we want to win the competition we have to win the games.

“Sometimes in this competition, it can happen that you play against big teams. It’s a great challenge for the players, for me, for our clubs. We have to arrive ready to play in our style, with personality, ready to play a game following the work we are doing on the training ground.”

A place in the League Cup third round is at stake as Tottenham host Charlton in a London derby at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. The last competitive meeting between these sides came in the FA Cup back in January 2011, with Tottenham winning that game 3-0 at White Hart Lane. A then 19-year-old Andros Townsend made his debut that day and scored, with Jermain Defoe scoring a brace.

Tottenham’s Premier League campaign got off to the worst possible start as they lost 3-0 at Brentford last weekend. Tottenham have been very busy during this summer transfer window and that has continued this week. Savio (formerly Savinho) has arrived from Manchester City in a deal that could be worth £85m and the Brazilian could make his Tottenham debut tonight, having been registered in time.

“I think in attacking positions we need players capable one-on one, to create something, to create a chance to score,” Roberto De Zerbi said. “In terms of one-on-one, he [Savio] is one of the best players, especially since 2024. He can play on the right side, on the left side. I have known him from a long time, I spoke with him when he went to Manchester City. He is a big player for us.

“I do not know if I am the right man [to get the most out of Savio], but for sure he has to achieve. I think a player who is so good in one-on-one, so good at creating chances to score, to be complete, he has to score. If you analyse the other best wingers in the world, many of them, they score 10 to 15 goals per season. He has the qualities. Maybe his habits, he has to change habits, because he has to be focused on the assists, the one-on-one dribbling and also to score.”

Omar Marmoush is closing in on an initial loan deal from Manchester City but that move is not complete and thus he is not available for Tottenham tonight. Micky van der Ven and Pedro Porro are both available having missed Tottenham’s loss at Brentford but the hosts are still without Xavi Simons, Pape Sarr, Dejan Kulusevski and Wilson Odobert.

Charlton have made the perfect start to their Championship campaign; a 2-1 home win over Derby was followed up by a 2-1 victory at recently-relegated West Ham. Nathan Jones’ side earned their place in the League Cup second round with a 3-1 win at Cheltenham in the first round.

“We have to be very organised and very professional, they [Tottenham] are a top team,” Jones said. “They have a great manager and a brilliant group of players. They already had a Premier League squad and they have spent, what is reaching about, I do not know, £300 million or something like that. It is a wonderful test, we have to be right near our best and do both sides of the game very well. Of course, you want to test yourself against the best managers and you want to test yourself against the best teams. For us, this is not our priority, the Championship is our priority, but this is the next game and therefore it is the most important.”

#1589. Czech Republic vs Spain - prediction, team news, lineups

By Matt Law | 10 Nov 2026 10:02, Last updated: 10 Nov 2026 10:04

Already-qualified Spain will continue their 2026-27 UEFA Nations League campaign with a contest against already-eliminated Czech Republic on Thursday night.

La Roja are currently top of Group A3, three points ahead of second-placed England, while Czech Republic are fourth, losing all four of their matches in the section.

There is no getting away from the fact that it has been a very difficult Nations League campaign for Czech Republic, who have lost each of their four matches in Group A3.

The Representatives started their 2026-27 campaign with a 2-1 home loss to Croatia, before going down 2-0 at home to England; a 3-1 defeat away to Spain followed, and the national team were then beaten 3-0 by England at Wembley last time out.

Santi Denia's side cannot qualify for the quarter-finals, and they are facing relegation to League B, although it is still possible for them to finish third in this section.

Czech Republic will travel to Croatia in their final game in the section on November 15, and it would be hugely disappointing for the national team if they finished the group without a point.

The Representatives have actually lost six of their last seven matches in all competitions, with their last victory coming in a friendly against Guatemala back in June.

Spain, meanwhile, are safely through to the quarter-finals of the tournament, although they are not yet certain of top position at this stage of proceedings.

La Roja have won all four of their matches in Group A3, scoring 12 goals in the process, and they ended the last international period with a 2-1 success over Croatia.

Luis de la Fuente's side, who won the World Cup in July, beat England 3-2 in their section opener before posting a 4-1 victory over Croatia and a 3-1 win over Czech Republic; Spain are the outstanding team in world football and are regarded as the favourites for the Nations League trophy.

La Roja have won each of their last 11 matches in all competitions, while they have not lost a single match in normal time since March 2024, although the national team were beaten on penalties by Portugal in the final of the 2025 Nations League.

Spain have never lost to Czech Republic, winning six of their previous eight meetings and drawing the other two, so history would be created if the hosts triumph on Thursday.

Czech Republic will be missing Michal Sadilek through suspension, but Ladislav Krejci is available again after serving a ban in the team's last fixture against England.

There should be a spot in the middle of the midfield for Tomas Soucek, who is in line to win his 94th cap for his country, while Vladimir Coufal is expected to feature for the 68th time for Czech Republic at the back.

Adam Hlozek has scored five times in 50 caps and is set to lead the line, while 18-year-old Idris Hopi will hope to make his senior international debut at some stage of the contest.

As for Spain, Lamine Yamal will not be involved, with the 19-year-old nursing a knee injury that he suffered while representing Barcelona against Atletico Madrid on Sunday.

Yamal is expected to link up with the Spain squad after this match, though, to prepare for the game against England on Sunday.

Mikel Oyarzabal will also be a notable absentee for De la Fuente's side due to illness.

Alex Baena and Fermin Lopez are one booking away from being suspended for the clash with England, but both are expected to be in the starting team against Czech Republic.

Kinsky; Coufal, Chaloupek, Krejci, Slama; Kral, Soucek; Cerv, Ambros, Danek; Hlozek

Simon; Porro, Cubarsi, Laporte, Cucurella; Pedri, Ruiz; N Williams, Fermin, Baena; Torres

Even without Yamal, Spain should be too strong for their opponents on Thursday - it has been a tough campaign for Czech Republic, and we are struggling to back them to secure a positive result here.

#1588. Tottenham are proof that a truckload of NFL and Beyonce cash is no use if you don't spend it properly, writes TOM COLLOMOSSE - after Roberto De Zerbi's £500m team saw their mini-revival ended by Leeds

Published: 09:34 EST, 7 November 2026 | Updated: 11:04 EST, 7 November 2026

Clubs outside European football’s elite are convinced the game’s financial rules are rigged to protect the richest and keep out the pretenders.

But Tottenham are living proof that making a truckload of money from Beyonce concerts and NFL fixtures is no use if you do not spend it properly.

A decade ago, Spurs fans complained frequently that Daniel Levy would not loosen the purse strings. At the time, the club was riding high under Mauricio Pochettino but could not take the final jump that – perhaps – a world-class signing or two would have delivered.

On reflection, perhaps the hierarchy were right back then. Maybe if they had worked within tighter limits in recent years, they might have made more sensible decisions in the market.

Tottenham’s starting XI at Leeds cost the best part of £500million with Leeds’ barely a quarter of that. It did not stop substitute Noah Okafor settling a tight game late in the second half and ending Spurs’ mini-revival.

Consider Pochettino’s Tottenham side at its peak. We’re not talking just Harry Kane, but Mousa Dembele, Kyle Walker, Christian Eriksen and Danny Rose. Hugo Lloris, Jan Vertonghen, Toby Alderweireld, Dele Alli and Heung-min Son.

Not many of the current crop would make it anywhere that team which is rather worrying when we consider the sums Tottenham have invested.

Leeds United leapfrogged Tottenham into the top half of the Premier League table

Roberto De Zerbi saw his side's three-game winning run come to an end at Elland Road

The problem with this squad is that they have a whole heap of players in the ‘good-to-very good’ bracket, who are largely interchangeable among themselves. A few, like Micky van de Ven, James Maddison, Sandro Tonali and potentially Mateus Fernandes, are a little above that category. There is nobody, though, who you could truly call world class.

Take Roberto De Zerbi, too. A bright, talented boss who did commendable work at Sassuolo, Shakhtar Donetsk, Brighton and Marseille. He does not, however, belong to the top rank like Pep Guardiola, Luis Enrique, Unai Emery or – increasingly – Mikel Arteta.

Here, Okafor scored the only goal barely a minute after coming on, combining with fellow sub Harry Wilson and slotting beyond Antonin Kinsky. Leeds made most of the chances in the second half and ended a five-match run without a win, though James Trafford saved Jan Paul van Hecke’s header late on to preserve the points.

Spurs have enough talent to keep them well clear of relegation and it is the kind of squad who can make a strong cup run. That is what Spurs have often been in modern times and there is nothing essentially wrong with it. Given the cash the current regime have splashed, though, they may just expect a little more.

Every summer, they do it. They tweak, fiddle and fuss. They preach about high bars, mic up officials and apologise to angry managers.

They have even changed the name of their organisation from PGMOL to Pro Ref, but they will never remove the controversy that VAR causes nearly every weekend.

Towards the end of the first half, Mathys Tel screamed in pain after Jayden Bogle fouled him. Replays showed Bogle’s studs make a solid contact with the Frenchman’s ankle but after nearly five minutes of checking, referee John Brooks was told to stick with his original decision.

‘Jayden is one of the fairest players in the country,’ said Leeds boss Daniel Farke. ‘He is more like a butterfly than an eagle and he would not even foul a player on purpose, let alone injure them. It was never intentional and maybe this is why the VAR said it was not a red card.’

Bogle escaped because there was ‘a lack of speed going into the challenge’ which VAR Tony Harrington deemed ‘reckless’ rather than dangerous. Whatever it was, Tel was injured moments later and Leeds had got away with one. Tel will have scans and De Zerbi fears the worst.

In real time, it looked a standard foul. After re-watching, though, it was hard to see how Bogle could stay on the pitch.

For all the decisions VAR overturns correctly, there are still far too many that leave too many people baffled.

‘I can’t say more as I didn’t see the situation clearly but I was surprised to see Pedro Porro given a yellow card in the second half for a foul in a similar position,’ said De Zerbi. ‘I don’t know if [Bogle’s] foul should be a red card or not but today the parameters of the referee were not good enough for these situations.’

Leeds are planning to expand Elland Road, but the stadium must not lose its raw essence

Leeds are working to increase the size of Elland Road and hope that the capacity will eventually be 53,000. Whatever they do, they must not damage the place’s raw essence.

Only Arsenal, Manchester City and Liverpool have a better points-per-game record than Leeds since Daniel Farke became boss in 2023. The lunchtime kick-off will never match the floodlit fixture for atmosphere but the second half here was as raucous as on its best days, and the stadium shook when Okafor slotted the winner past Antonin Kinsky.

‘When you have a few games without the winning feeling, it’s always difficult,’ Farke admitted. ‘Heading into the international break, it’s important to win again.’

There is plenty to improve for Leeds. If Dominic Calvert-Lewin catches a cold, where do the goals come from? Who can replace what Ethan Ampadu provides in the centre of midfield?

These are questions for Farke to tackle but with Elland Road at his team’s back, he has solid foundations on which to build.

Leeds (3-5-2): Trafford 6; Justin 7, Elvedi 7, MUHAREMOVIC 8; Bogle 7 (Rodon 90+3), Longstaff 6 (Gruev 90+2), Ampadu 7, Tanaka 6 (Wilson 77), Gudmundsson 7 (Bard 46, 7); Calvert-Lewin 7, Nmecha 6 (Okafor 77).

#1587. Spalletti open to 3-4-2-1 at Genoa but expects few changes with Napoli next

Luciano Spalletti is ready to shift from a 3-5-2 to a 3-4-2-1 at Genoa, with Alajbegovic among the options behind the striker. With eight players injured and Napoli due on Sunday, he expects his team to stay broadly the same.

Luciano Spalletti is ready to tweak his shape at Genoa without tearing up his team. On the eve of the trip, the Juventus coach said one very small positional change turns the 3-5-2 into a 3-4-2-1. Anyone, he added, can fill the two roles behind the striker.

He named Alajbegovic, Boga and Zhegrova as options in that zone. Kolo Muani was his example of the profile he has in mind. Spalletti said the forward can play partly as a number 10 and partly as a wide forward. Sarr has recovered and is available.

Tuttosport expects Alajbegovic to possibly replace Kolo Muani behind Woltemade, and sees Cambiaso as the only left-flank option with Celik injured.

The fixture list explains the caution. The trip to Genoa is the first of two games in five days. Spalletti is weighing a few rotations partly because of the second of those games, Sky Sport reported. Asked about Napoli, the coach said everything has to be taken into account. He still expects the team to stay broadly the same.

Spalletti also said his players are fully focused and have the right mentality. That follows a mixed run. Juventus lost at home to Lazio on 18 October. Afterwards Spalletti said his side had shown fragility that starts in the mind. He added that tactical systems change nothing without hunger, passion, courage and character. A draw with Rennes followed.

The win at Lecce began to make up for both results. McKennie volleyed in a Douglas Luiz free kick in the 29th minute. Douglas Luiz added the second four minutes before half-time.

Spalletti described Genoa as an extremely hard opponent, citing both the atmosphere at their ground and their tactics. He warned they can use their physical strength at set pieces and also run in behind defences. Above all, he said, the side carries Daniele De Rossi’s fighting spirit.

The warning on dead balls fits recent meetings between the clubs. Six of the last ten goals between the clubs came from set pieces: two from corners, one from a throw-in and three from penalties.

#1584. Spalletti apologises after Genoa defeat leaves Juventus level with Napoli on 14 points

Juventus lost 2-0 at Genoa on Serie A Matchday 9, a third league defeat in nine games that undid the good work of the win at Lecce. Napoli, the next visitors to Turin, now have the same points total.

The defeat came on 28 October 2026, with both Genoa goals arriving before half-time. Luciano Spalletti apologised to the supporters afterwards. The result came three days after a 2-0 win at Lecce on Matchday 8. That win, built on first-half goals from Weston McKennie and Douglas Luiz, now looks like a false dawn.

Genoa needed little time to break through, and Ehizibue was the man to do it. His goal ended a 504-minute run without a Genoa goal against Juventus in Serie A, going back to an Albert Gudmundsson strike on 15 December 2023, Sportmediaset reported.

Baldanzi then exposed the Juventus defence again. Scoring and setting up a goal in one Serie A match was new for Baldanzi.

Juventus’s best chance of the first half came just before the interval. Kalulu shot off target after a pass from McKennie. Spalletti sent on Edon Zhegrova and Nick Woltemade for the second half. The changes did not help, and Genoa held firm. The win moved Daniele De Rossi’s side up to 10 points.

The coach did not hide from the performance. His team were beaten in every area of the pitch and must improve physically and in their fighting spirit, Spalletti told the club’s website. In his press conference he pointed to a lack of physical impact and to lost duels.

He also noted that the level shown at Lecce had not been repeated. There had been no training session between the two matches. That short turnaround is part of his explanation.

The evening got worse elsewhere. Napoli won 4-1 at Monza, with goals from Højlund, Politano, Rafa Marín and De Bruyne. Their coach, Massimiliano Allegri, watched from the stands. He was serving a two-match ban picked up against Roma.

Spalletti described Napoli as a very strong team. Both sides sit well behind the top of the table, so the meeting carries weight for each.

— JuventusFC (@juventusfc) October 28, 2026

The response he wants will have to come quickly, with little time to work on the training ground. A home crowd that received an apology on Wednesday will be watching closely.

#1583. Liverpool: Hungary confirm "last-minute" Dominik Szoboszlai decision in new injury update

By Ben Knapton | 10 Nov 2026 10:12

Liverpool midfielder Dominik Szoboszlai will remain with the Hungary national team following medical examinations, the Magyars have announced.

The 26-year-old arrived for the November international break carrying a knee injury, which he sustained in Liverpool's 3-1 win over Crystal Palace in the Premier League on Sunday.

Andoni Iraola admitted at full time that Szoboszlai was not feeling 100%, although the former RB Leipzig man nevertheless joined up with his compatriots for the UEFA Nations League.

Hungary issued a statement on Monday morning announcing that Szoboszlai would undergo further medical tests on his knee sprain, which have now been completed, and he will not be sent back to Kirkby.

However, in a fresh update on Tuesday, Hungary also conceded that they are unlikely to make any decisions on Szoboszlai's involvement until the very last minute.

"Dominik Szoboszlai has undergone the required medical examinations. Following his knee sprain, the national team’s medical staff will do everything possible over the coming days to ensure that the team captain is available to the coaching staff as soon as possible," the statement read.

"However, a decision on his availability for the match will almost certainly only be made at the last minute."

Hungary face Georgia in their penultimate Nations League group-stage game on Saturday, before also taking on Northern Ireland next Tuesday in League B Group 2.

The Magyars currently sit second in the group with seven points from four games, one point adrift of leaders Northern Ireland in top spot, which guarantees promotion to League A.

Hungary's second-placed ranking would see Szoboszlai's side advance to the promotion playoffs, where they would meet a third or fourth-placed team from League A for the right to progress to the top tier.

Szoboszlai came back from the September/October international break with a hamstring injury, which he then exacerbated against Brentford, causing him to miss five games in total for Liverpool so far this season.

As Hungary are vying for League A promotion, and Szoboszlai is arguably their most important player, the Magyars' decision to keep the midfielder around for now is both understandable and defensible.

Liverpool fans will no doubt want the midfielder to withdraw, return to Merseyside and enjoy a complete rest over the international break, and that scenario could still occur if his knee issue flares up over the coming days.

However, Szoboszlai should also do everything in his power to make himself available for his country, thereby forcing Liverpool fans to watch on anxiously over the next week.

Belarus make the trip to San Marino on Thursday evening looking for the win that could see them end the night sitting in top spot of Group C1 in the UEFA Nations League.

Meanwhile, San Marino head into the game in Serravalle assured of bottom spot having lost all four of their matches.

As far as San Marino are concerned, they will be bitterly disappointed to have conceded 16 goals across four matches at this level.

San Marino will make at least two changes for this fixture, a consequence of centre-back Michele Cevoli being left out of the squad due to injury and striker Nicolas Giacopetti serving a one-match ban.

Lorenzo Lazarri is an alternative in midfield having scored as a substitute in Albania.

With Belarus duo Artem Shumanskiy and German Barkovskiy serving one-match bans, Artem Kontsevoy and Vitaliy Lisakovich may be drafted into the final third.

#1581. Key adjustments and becoming possession-oriented: Tactical analysis of Genoa 1-2 AC Milan

AC Milan climbed back into the top four in the Serie A table with a much-needed win away against Genoa before the international break.

Milan found themselves two goals up inside 20 minutes when Alphadjo Cisse slotted in a cut-back from Adrien Rabiot and Christian Pulisic buried a square pass from Gonçalo Ramos, with both goals coming from the high press.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

However, it wouldn’t be the Rossoneri without some late drama, and Ellertsson made it a very nervy finish for the Rossoneri with a goal inside the final few minutes from a long-range strike. Milan did manage to hang on for what was an important three points.

Como’s defeat to Inter means that Ruben Amorim’s men move into the Champions League places, though after the break the pursuit of consistency will continue. Below is the tactical breakdown, from Rohit Rajeev.

Amorim chose to make five changes from Thursday’s defeat to Ferencvaros. Mike Maignan, Mario Gila, Luka Modric, Diego Moreira and Christian Pulisic all came into the side, though there were some question marks about whether it would be a four or three-man defence based on the names selected.

Genoa’s direct approach immediately put Milan on the back foot, with the hosts threatening to exploit the space behind the defensive line in the opening minute.

They played a long ball into the space behind Koni De Winter, allowing Osmanjic to run in behind and chase the delivery. Although the move appeared to be offside, it served as an early warning of the threat Genoa’s direct approach could pose to Milan’s defence.

Genoa anticipated Milan’s tendency to create numerical overloads in the wide areas and adjusted their defensive structure accordingly.

They used the corresponding centre-back, wing-back and both players from the double pivot to create a 4v3 numerical superiority against Milan’s wide combinations.

This allowed Genoa to outnumber Milan’s attacking players, restrict their progression down the flanks and make it difficult for Amorim’s side to exploit their usual wide overloads.

Milan’s in-possession structure alternated between a 4-1-4-1 and a 3-1-4-2, with the positioning of Musah largely determining which shape the team adopted.

Rabiot occupied the left half-space, while Pulisic preferred to operate closer to Moreira on the right. Meanwhile, Cisse provided the width on the left flank, functioning as Milan’s left winger.

Milan operated with a vertically staggered double pivot, comprising Modric and Rabiot. Modric occupied the deeper position, acting as the midfield screen in front of the back four and providing a link between defence and midfield.

Rabiot, meanwhile, operated higher up the pitch, effectively taking on the role of an attacking midfielder and providing an additional presence between Genoa’s midfield and defensive lines.

The move leading to Cisse’s goal began with Vasquez being tasked with progressing possession from the back. However, Milan managed to create a 3v4 numerical disadvantage for Genoa in the wide areas, forcing Vasquez to recycle possession rather than progress the ball.

Pulisic recognised the opportunity to press and initiated a ball-oriented press, eventually dispossessing Vasquez. He immediately released Rabiot, allowing Milan to exploit the turnover before Genoa could reorganise defensively.

As the possession changed hands, Ramos scanned his surroundings and identified Cisse’s position, recognising the opportunity to attack the space inside the penalty area.

Milan subsequently created a 3v2 numerical advantage inside the box. Cisse initially ran alongside Ramos before checking his run to deceive Marcandalli. This subtle change of movement created separation from his marker and allowed him to attack the space.

Rabiot delivered the cross into the penalty area, where Cisse was perfectly positioned to finish the move and give Milan the lead.

Although Milan adopted a high, man-oriented pressing structure, there were gaps that Genoa could exploit during their build-up. Musah, conscious of the possibility of Genoa creating a 2v1 situation, chose to stay closer to Diawara rather than move out to engage the ball carrier.

This left Ezhibue free to receive possession in the sizeable gap between Musah and Cisse, exposing a weakness in Milan’s pressing structure.

The move leading to Milan’s second goal began with Cisse pressing Traore from behind as the Genoa defender approached the goal line.

Under pressure, Traore attempted a cross-field pass, but Ramos positioned himself intelligently to block the passing lane towards Vasquez.

Rather than attempting to finish the move himself, Ramos showed excellent composure and unselfishly squared the ball into Pulisic’s path, despite Moreira also calling for the pass.

What made the assist particularly impressive was the Portuguese’s execution: he played a no-look pass, deceiving both the goalkeeper and the recovering defender about his intended target. Pulisic capitalised on the opportunity and converted the chance to double Milan’s advantage.

With each passing game Milan are moving into a pure possession-oriented team. In this sequence you can see Pulisic and Rabiot exchanging their positions to confuse their markers

With a 2-0 advantage, Milan shifted towards a more conservative approach, prioritising defensive stability over attacking progression. Amorim reorganised the side into a 5-4-1 defensive structure, adding greater protection to the backline and reducing the spaces available for Genoa to exploit.

However, one of the inherent vulnerabilities of a five-man defensive structure is the space left behind the wing-backs when they are drawn towards the ball.

Genoa looked to exploit this weakness by deliberately dragging Moreira out of his defensive position. As Moreira stepped forward to engage the ball carrier, Gila was forced to jump out of the defensive line to prevent Genoa from creating a 2v1 situation.

This movement consequently opened up space in the right channel, allowing Genoa to exploit an area that would otherwise have been protected by Milan’s compact 5-4-1 defensive block.

Genoa switched from their initial 3-4-2-1 to a 4-4-2 formation as they looked to change their attacking approach. El Shaarawy moved into the left midfield position, Vitinha operated on the right, while Baldanzi took up the role of a second striker.

The substitution of Marcandalli also prompted a structural change at the back, with Genoa abandoning their back three in favour of a back four. Ekhator moved into the right-back position, allowing Genoa to maintain a more conventional defensive structure.

For Genoa’s goal, Milan failed to close down Ellertsson, with the defenders seemingly anticipating a cross rather than a shot. Ellertsson recognised the opportunity and noticed that Maignan’s line of sight was obstructed by four Milan defenders.

Taking advantage of the goalkeeper’s limited visibility, he opted to shoot rather than deliver a cross, finding the back of the net.

#1580. Inside Oliver Glasner's Forest struggles: Unserious players who act like superstars when they don't deserve to, alarming physical data - and squad's grumbles revealed

Published: 12:00 EST, 2 November 2026 | Updated: 13:25 EST, 7 November 2026

If football management were gambling, Oliver Glasner has just done the equivalent of walking into one of Nottingham’s top casinos and chucking everything on red.

Not satisfied with hammering his Forest players publicly after Saturday’s 2-0 defeat at Brentford, Glasner then had the squad running on the banks of the River Trent for their customary Sunday recovery session. The social media footage has to be seen to be believed – Premier League footballers jogging through an overgrown field, filmed by a baffled dog-walker.

Even if Forest were doing well and their players were easy to manage, these would still be risky moves. Instead, Glasner's side are 19th in the table and he is trying to handle a notoriously restless dressing room.

Forest are believed to pay Glasner more than £10million a year and until now owner Evangelos Marinakis has been patient. But in the Premier League most fans are sceptical when club officials talk about long-term projects and three-year plans. Only three of the current 20 managers have lasted three years in their current job.

Any manager who loses regularly is under pressure, particularly at a club who sacked three managers last season and another in the summer. Glasner has lost six of 10 as Forest boss and won only once. Forget the spin: results alone mean Glasner is under the pump.

If there are no signs of a reaction against Manchester City on Saturday, it promises to be an uncomfortable November international break.

If there are no signs of a Nottingham Forest reaction against Man City on Saturday, it promises to be an uncomfortable November international break for Oliver Glasner

There was not one single moment that broke Glasner’s patience but the 30th minute at Brentford on Saturday probably contributed heavily.

Forest centre back Murillo, who has regressed alarmingly this season, watched idly as Bees goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher launched the ball way over his head and into the path of Dango Ouattara. Ouattara then breezed past Murillo before Nikola Milenkovic turned the cross into his own net. Glasner was unhappy with the shape Murillo was in when he returned for pre-season training and was furious at such slack work.

It was not the first time Forest had been exposed like this, either. Jay Dasilva’s winner for Coventry at the City Ground in September came from a similar diagonal pass from keeper Carl Rushworth, though that time Daniel Munoz – one of Glasner’s pupils – was at fault. Again, slack. Again, sloppy.

Daily Mail Sport understands Glasner does not see enough seriousness in his squad. This group of players get on well but nonetheless, there is a view that poor results do not hurt them enough. Is it really time for laughing and joking around the training ground when you have taken one point from a possible 15?

Most of this squad have never won a European trophy, or one in Europe’s top five leagues. Glasner has three. Some around him believe there are Forest players who carry themselves like superstars when they do not deserve to.

It is thought Glasner is also frustrated with himself. Looking back, perhaps he wishes he had started with a bang, because the 52-year-old was alarmed at the physical data from previous seasons.

In 2024-25, Forest covered fewer kilometres than any other team, and last season only Liverpool and Chelsea covered fewer. In 2024-25, only Arsenal made fewer sprints; last season, only Everton were below Forest. Glasner’s Palace sides were never lower than 12th in those four categories.

When Glasner has been outspoken in the past, it has usually worked. At Wolfsburg and Frankfurt, performances improved. At Crystal Palace last season, Glasner let rip at his bosses after a game at Sunderland last January and most expected him to be sacked. Instead, he left in the summer after delivering the Conference League. The dynamic at Forest is very different though – and Glasner may soon understand why.

Glasner was unhappy with the shape Murillo (left) was in when he returned for pre-season training and was furious at the Brazilian's slack work at Brentford

Player power was a major factor in Ange Postecoglou and Sean Dyche's sackings last season. When players believe they can go above the manager’s head and vent to those in charge, they will. This is the danger for Glasner.

Daily Mail Sport understands there are players who love neither the new style – Glasner is a committed three-at-the-back man and many of the squad feel more comfortable in a back-four – nor the Austrian’s strict approach. He is very different from the avuncular Vitor Pereira, whose easy charm and light-touch approach united the squad post-Dyche and kept Forest in the top flight.

Others are surprised Glasner has not made it a priority to bring the dressing room’s strongest characters onside. Along with Morgan Gibbs-White, both Ola Aina and Callum Hudson-Odoi are powerful voices in the squad and alienating any of them is dangerous. Equally, Ibrahim Sangare and Nico Dominguez are well-respected, and both have been left on the fringes like Aina and Hudson-Odoi.

While Gibbs-White is clearly Forest’s best player, he can be a complex character. If the skipper is not 'having’ a Forest manager, his position becomes vulnerable.

It was a turbulent summer for Gibbs-White, who was frustrated no Champions League club came in for him and ultimately changed agents. He was also left out of England’s World Cup squad. Some believe that Glasner’s rigid tactical framework does not bring the best from Gibbs-White, who likes to roam across the front line and drop deep when he wishes. While Pereira understood this, Glasner does not operate like that.

At times this season, Gibbs-White’s body language has been striking. Team-mates who make mistakes feel his anger but the 26-year-old has only one goal (a penalty) and two assists this term.

Gibbs-White watched team-mate Elliot Anderson leave Forest for City last summer and perhaps questioned why he was not on the same path to the Champions League.

It is tempting to wonder about some of the advice Gibbs-White has received from those around him, though. Because if Gibbs-White is wondering why he is still playing for a bottom-half Premier League club, it is never a bad idea to look in the mirror.

Callum Hudson-Odoi is a powerful voice in the dressing room and Glasner would do well not to isolate him

If  Morgan Gibbs-White is wondering why he is still playing for a bottom-half Premier League club, it is never a bad idea to look in the mirror

Marinakis did not make Glasner the highest-paid manager in Forest’s history just to show him the door at the first sign of trouble. When the pair held talks, Glasner is thought to have stressed the need for time to make his vision work.

Neither man suffers fools and it is easy to imagine that Marinakis would have approved of parts of Glasner’s outburst. That does not give Glasner a free pass, because Marinakis factored in player feeling when dismissing Postecoglou and Dyche.

If the Glasner experiment fails, George Syrianos will come under scrutiny. Forest’s chief football officer has more power at the club than at any other time and he pushed hard for Glasner, whom he has known for some time through links to German football.

It is believed the pair had some contact over possible transfer business during Glasner’s time at Palace, and Glasner would likely have welcomed the chance to work with Syrianos at Selhurst Park.

In December 2023, Syrianos wanted Glasner to replace Steve Cooper but Marinakis chose Nuno Espirito Santo instead. Marinakis’ son, Miltiadis, is at the training ground regularly and will report back to his father. These are testing times for Glasner and his champion.

Dyche has had his say, too. During a poor run of results last season, he gathered the Forest players and staff for their views on what needed to change.

Anticipating their opinions on formations and tactics, Dyche was bewildered when one player queried the decision to move the weekly barber visit from Friday to Thursday. Nevertheless, that player is still at Forest and Dyche lasted less than four months.

Dyche  made many mistakes at Forest but his latest posts on Threads felt relevant.

If the Glasner experiment fails, George Syrianos will come under scrutiny. Forest’s chief football officer has more power at the club than ever before and he pushed hard for Glasner

The problem at Forest is that even if the players fail to stand up and be counted, they are rarely the ones to pay the ultimate price

They read: ‘The badge is bigger than all… and yet it seems not nowadays! I can only hope it turns and the culture we were insisting upon is now being assessed and realised as what was and is needed. Oliver is out there saying what I was saying… in his own style.

‘Nottingham Forest are still finding the goals hard to come by – and I had it along with my staff – we scored but nowhere near what the metrics were telling us, so not enough to stay in our job?

'We had 35 efforts at goal v Wolves and yet a 0-0 result and it culminated in myself and staff being sacked. I hope Oliver is given more time, the fans stay with him and the players stand up and be counted.'

The problem at Forest is that even if the players fail to do so, they are rarely the ones to pay the ultimate price.

#1579. Germany squad: Five players to watch under Jurgen Klopp this month including 17-year-old wunderkind

By Oliver Thomas | 10 Nov 2026 10:20

Germany head coach Jurgen Klopp has drastically trimmed his squad ahead of two crucial UEFA Nations League fixtures against Serbia and the Netherlands during the November international break.

Facing a must-win double-header, Die Mannschaft are in danger of failing to qualify for the quarter-finals as they currently sit third in League A Group C, three points behind both of their upcoming opponents.

Germany will first travel to Belgrade to face Serbia on Friday, before returning home to host the Netherlands in a blockbuster clash at the Olympiastadion in Berlin next Monday.

From history-making teenage playmakers to reborn Bundesliga stars and Premier League luminaries, Klopp's 24-man squad is a fascinating blend of elite experience and explosive youth.

These two crunch matches present the ultimate stage for several international hopefuls to cement their place under Klopp, and here, Sports Mole takes a closer look at five Germany players to watch out for during this month's international break.

The surprise inclusion to Klopp’s latest squad is Borussia Monchengladbach’s wunderkind Wael Mohya, who has earned his first-ever senior call-up for Germany ahead of his 18th birthday next month.

The 2008 Mettmann-born starlet, who is of Moroccan descent through his parents, broke into Monchengladbach’s senior team midway through last season and became the club’s youngest-ever goalscorer against Bayern Munich in March of this year.

He has since been linked with the likes of Bayern and Liverpool in recent months, having developed into an increasingly influential figure under head coach Alexander Blessin this term, featuring in all nine Bundesliga games as well as two DFB-Pokal matches.

Mohya became the fourth youngest-player in Bundesliga history to score in back-to-back matches last month, contributing with a goal and an assist in a standout display in a 3-2 victory over Stuttgart – Monchengladbach’s only league win of the season to date.

The dynamic teenage attacker, comfortable operating centrally and as a winger on either flank, is blessed with superb close control and an innate ability to operate comfortably with both feet, offering Klopp a highly creative, versatile midfield weapon.

Mohya, who has received eight Germany youth caps between Under-16 and Under-21 level, is undeniably one to watch this month as he bids to become the third-youngest senior international in German history and bring his fearless club form onto the Nations League stage.

An explosive start to the 2026-27 campaign by striker Niclas Fullkrug has been rewarded with a return to the Germany national team squad for the first time since September 2025.

The veteran marksman endured difficult spells at both West Ham United and AC Milan, but he is enjoying a remarkable revival on loan at Werder Bremen, where he began his career 15 years ago.

At the age of 33, Fullkrug has proven that age is just a number by plundering a ruthless nine goals in as many Bundesliga appearances so far this season, firing him to the top of the division’s scoring charts and already five clear of Ballon d’Or winner Harry Kane.

Fullkrug’s lethal aerial presence and old-school, back-to-goal physical profile offer Germany a genuine focal point with qualities that differ to both Kai Havertz and Younes Ebnoutalib who will also battle for the No.9 role under Klopp.

If Germany are to breach the backlines of Serbia and the Netherlands this month, Fullkrug's predatory instincts inside the penalty area could be paramount should he be selected to lead the line.

Having made his senior international debut under Klopp during the previous window, Koln’s crown jewel has done more than enough to maintain his place in this refined 24-man squad.

The highly-rated 20-year-old winger has seamlessly transitioned his dominant youth form into the Bundesliga, contributing to 18 goals (13 goals, five assists) in 34 top-flight matches last season to help Koln avoid relegation.

This term, El Mala has found the net five times in 10 appearances in all competitions, including a late consolation strike against Bayer Leverkusen last weekend, and his strong performances continue to be monitored by a number of Europe’s biggest clubs.

Boasting rare physical traits for a wide player at 6ft 2in, El Mala pairs raw explosive pace with clinical goalscoring instincts, and his ability to drive vertically at opposing full-backs provides a unique dynamic to a German attack that has typically favoured shorter, intricate passing combinations.

With Klopp eager to establish a permanent threat on the flanks, El Mala represents a intriguing tactical alternative for this month's double-header while the likes of Karim Adeyemi, Serge Gnabry, Leroy Sane, Chris Fuhrich, Jamie Leweling and Kevin Schade all watch on from afar.

Having initially been left out of Klopp’s squad, Ridle Baku has received a late call-up to the Germany set-up after Waldemar Anton was forced to withdraw over the weekend due to injury.

The right-back has played 12 times for a Leipzig side who sit fourth in the Bundesliga table and has chipped in with three goals, with his qualities on full display in a narrow Champions League defeat to Man City last week in which he fired home a second-half equaliser.

The 28-year-old right-back has not featured for the national team since earning his eighth cap in November last year, but this window offers a massive opportunity for him to revitalise his international career.

Baku will face stern competition for starts at right-back from Freiburg's Philipp Treu who was preferred for the previous international window and made a notable impression during his maiden Germany outing.

However, having two strong right-back options battling it out against each other would enable Klopp to continue with captain Joshua Kimmich as a central midfielder, where his tactical intelligence and elite passing range can orchestrate the play.

In the absence of injured star Jamal Musiala, Liverpool’s Florian Wirtz carries the creative burden for Klopp’s Germany side and will hope to transfer his recent form at club level onto the international stage.

Wirtz has previously come under fire for failing to make the desired impact at Liverpool, but he ranks joint-second for chances created in the Premier League so far this season (22) and has contributed to four goals in his last four top-flight appearances.

After setting up goals in wins over Brighton and Brentford, Wirtz scored and assisted in Liverpool’s 3-1 victory at Crystal Palace last weekend, helping Andoni Iraola’s side climb back into the top four.

At 23 years of age, Wirtz is in fact one of the more experienced players in Klopp’s squad, as his 48 international caps is only bettered by three players (Kimmich, Havertz and Jonathan Tah).

Having captained Germany in their last Nations League match, Wirtz will be tasked with orchestrating the offensive tempo from the number 10 role as the battle for knockout qualification reaches a boiling point.

He will aim to replicate his man-of-the-match display in last month's 2-0 win over Serbia in which he scored and assisted.
