#1495. Martin Odegaard sends Arsenal six clear at the top: The stylists and aesthetes will moan - but Mikel Arteta can rest easy over the international break, writes RIATH AL-SAMARRAI

By RIATH AL-SAMARRAI, CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER

Published: 12:30 EST, 7 November 2026 | Updated: 19:22 EST, 7 November 2026

Arsenal are building a wall around their precious trophy with ugly bricks. While the stylists and aesthetes among us can moan about such details, a quick glance at the league table will be sufficient for Mikel Arteta to rest easy during the international break.

There are certainly things for him to improve. Masses of them. And we can all share the disappointment that the sum of such gifted parts is often quite underwhelming. There's a relentlessness about that conversation.

But Arsenal are relentless in other ways, too. Which is to say they are finding ways to win, with this their ninth in ten games and arguably the least convincing of an unconvincing bunch.

If Manchester City weren't facing up to the possibility of an apocalyptic punishment, those performances would likely cause greater concern but it's a tangential argument. A purist's debate. And by extension it is pointless against the single factor that matters most – scoring more than the other lot.

In this case, grimy as it was, that crowning role fell to Martin Odegaard, who nudged the winner over the line in the 72nd minute after benefiting from a favourable rebound after Konstantinos Tzolakis had saved from Noni Madueke.

The latter is surfing ever faster on the wave of his current form and impressed throughout this match, but his wing play and the resilience of Arteta's back four warranted isolated praise.

Martin Odegaard secured Arsenal's fourth Premier League win in succession against Hull

The Gunners had been frustrated by the newly-promoted side before Odegaard pounced

For all of Arsenal's grumbles about the officiating, including a bizarre penalty claim for Kai Havertz in the first half, they were poor, even if most sides would trade an arm for four straight clean sheets and a healthy lead in the table.

Arsenal (4-2-3-1): Raya 6; Timber 7, Konsa 7, Gabriel 6, Calafiori 7 (Hincapie 69, 7); Rice 6 (Merino 63, 7), Guimaraes 5 (Zubimendi 89); Madueke 8, Odegaard 7, Tzolis 5 (Eze 69, 6); Havertz 5 (Gyokeres 63, 6)

Subs not used: Arrizabalaga, White, Mosquera, Lewis-Skelly

Hull (5-3-2-): Tzolakis 7; Coyle 6 (Norton-Cuffy 60, 5), Ajayi 7 (Herrington 69, 6), Egan 7, Mendy 6, Stroud 7 (Giles 75, 6); Iroegbunam 7 (Mouzakitis 75, 6), Gourna-Douath 7, Slater 7; McBurnie 6, Cho 5 (Gelhardt 60, 6)

Subs not used: Butland, Giles, Thomas, Hjerto-Dahl, Vaz

For the majority of the first 45 minutes, this game was shaped by Hull, who hadn't won since August. They had drawn five of their previous seven games and given up winning positions in four of them, but Sergej Jakirovic is doing good work. Here, he had Arteta baffled for long stretches and elements of his blueprint will have been noted by future opposition.

Jakirovic's intentions had been clear, both on the team sheet and the pitch. He kept with his default setting for a back five, but switched from a 5-4-1 to 5-3-2 and introduced Mohamed-Ali Cho to partner Oli McBurnie in attack.

It was the first time this season that Hull's manager has used a front two and dovetailed with his midweek warning that camping on the edge of their area would lead nowhere but trouble. Instead, the aim was to squeeze, suffocate and chase the champions at every turn. That worked for an hour for Leeds and it did likewise for Hull.

Inside the first 70 seconds, they had forced a corner. A moment later, John Egan outjumped Gabriel Magalhaes and headed into the side netting.

Soon enough, David Raya was forced into a save by Regan Slater. In landing a shot on target, Hull had achieved a greater threat after 18 minutes than Liverpool delivered in the entire 90 at Anfield last weekend.

It was strong stuff. And ballsy. Arsenal had space to exploit at the other end but that was contingent on having the composure to pick the right pass. For an awfully long time, that eluded them.

Christos Tzolis and Havertz each offered the limpest of protests for early penalties and Declan Rice belatedly caused some threat with a half-volley. For a while, that was as good as it got, before a third penalty appeal arrived. This one was contentious.

Arsenal were denied a penalty following a shirt pull on centre forward Kai Havertz

Mikel Arteta demands a free kick in Arsenal's favour on a frustrating afternoon in north London

Mikel Arteta warned that Arsenal must be more 'chaotic' and ruthless after wasting multiple chances in their 1-0 victory over Hull City.

Martin Odegaard's second-half strike sealed a fifth consecutive Premier League victory for the Gunners going into the international break, though his side were initially frustrated by the stubborn visitors.

'I'm delighted with the win because to go into the international break after winning is one of the best things for a coach or a player,' said Arteta.

'I think we were the better team and had enough chances to make the scoreline much bigger. We weren't efficient enough to do that.

'We need to find ways to be more efficient, sometimes even more pragmatic.

'Sometimes my feeling is that we are trying to score a perfect goal against these low blocks. We need to be much more chaotic than that, and that's it. And score much earlier because obviously that's going to change the course of the game.'

Arsenal also had a penalty shout turned down in the first period after Kai Havertz's shirt was pulled in the box by Nobel Mendy.

The decision was not given on field, though the VAR told referee Farai Hallam to look at the pitchside monitor.

Hallam announced that Havertz had been fouled, but the forward had been in an offside position.

On the incident, Arteta said: 'I haven't watched it back. I was surprised because when they sent the referee to the monitor, Benji (White) was telling me it's a clear penalty.

'So I heard now that they decided not to (give a penalty) because of the starting position of Kai, that he was offside. So I don't know what the interpretation is. I'm sure they (Pro Ref) will make that clear to understand it.

'I need to understand the decision, what is overruling what in terms of the decision making and after that I can give you an answer.'

The offence traced to a clear shirt-pull by Nobel Mendy on Havertz, with referee Farai Hallam subsequently called to the screen to check if it merited a foul. Returning to the field and engaging his microphone, he confirmed it did but added that Havertz was in an offside position. The verdict: a Hull free-kick.

A word on Hallam – he was the referee who also overruled the VAR on his Premier League debut last season. It's good to see an official who backs his own judgment, so fair play, but was he in the right?

Such is the mess engulfing the laws on offside, an argument could be put forward that, according to the regulations, the foul must take precedence over the offside as Havertz wasn't yet challenging for the ball. A counterpoint: it's an absurd law that is far too subjective.

None of which helped Arsenal, of course. Not for the first time, they were struggling to utilise their creative talents, with Rice and Odegaard swamped in the middle and their supply lines to Tzolis almost non-existent. Madueke created his own threats, but with limited support. When Havertz had a decent opening late in the half, he took one touch too many and allowed Mendy to challenge. It was bleak.

Kicking his heels on the bench was Viktor Gyokeres, who had one of his finest Arsenal performances at Slavia Prague on Wednesday. His reward for a goal and an assist was one of those soul-crushing demotions for Premier League business, and he wasn't introduced here for more than an hour.

By then, Arsenal had asserted some control. Tzolis was drawing countless fouls, including one from Lewie Coyle that ought to have drawn a second yellow card as Hull's pressure strayed closer to brute force. Their grip on a point was loosening.

First, Madueke drew a save from Tzolakis and then he forced another after skipping around Elliot Stroud and pulling the trigger. This one proved decisive because the save rebounded to Odegaard. He poached the winner.

Madueke then ought to have killed the match, but opted to round Tzolakis instead of taking on the shot when through. The keeper won that battle; Arsenal won the game. Ultimately, not much else mattered.

#1494. How would Man Utd line-up if Mauricio Pochettino becomes manager?

According to reports, Mauricio Pochettino has edged ahead as the leading candidate to take over the mess at Manchester United.

Reports on Monday night suggested that Michael Carrick would soon face the sack and while names such as Eddie Howe have been linked, the current USMNT boss has emerged as the front runner.

But what would a Pochettino United team look like? How would it be different to Howe? Here’s our best guess.

One of the key components of Pochettino’s attacking philosophy is full-backs playing a major role in attacks. This will be a problem at United.

At Southampton, he had a young Luke Shaw and Nathaniel Clyne. Spurs were blessed with plenty of good full-backs in Danny Rose, Kyle Walker and Kieran Trippier.

All of these were young, athletic and attack-minded full-backs who could get up and down the wing and play a crucial role in going forward without being left so far forward that they cannot help at the back.

United’s full-back department is one of the poorest areas of the club. Pochettino has the options of his former player Shaw, who can’t stay fit, Noussair Mazraoui who lacks the engine to get up and down and Diogo Dalot who has one mistake in him per game at least.

When negotiating his contract, Pochettino would do well to insist that United strengthen this area during the winter transfer window.

Centrally, Pochettino insists that his teams play out of the back and so he will favour centre-backs that can do that.

Currently, Ayden Heaven and Lisandro Martinez are the best passing centre-back duo, averaging around 60 per game while Harry Maguire is at 51.6. Leny Yoro is down at 41.6.

In central midfield, Pochettino does not want his two defensive-minded players to simply win the ball but also be able to create as well. Harry Winks, Christian Eriksen and Mamadou Sissoko all played in that double pivot and all three could be classed as good on the ball as well as winning it back.

Seemingly perfect for that role is Kobbie Mainoo who has made the most defensive contributions per 90 and accurate passes per 90 of anyone in the United squad.

Alongside Mainoo, Pochettino would likely rotate between Andre Onana and Youri Tielemans depending on the opponent.

At Spurs, Pochettino was blessed with a young Harry Kane who had all the potential to become a Ballon d’Or winner. He is not going to find similar quality at United.

A player with the profile of Kane would work perfectly for United as it would allow Bruno Fernandes to crash into the box and score goals but United lack that type of player. Pochettino will have to work with Joshua Zirkzee until January at the earliest.

Two players that would likely benefit from a Pochettino system is Bryan Mbeumo and Matheus Cunha.

While Howe likes his wingers to hug the touchline before cutting in late, Pochettino likes to play attacking midfielders in his wide positions and encourage them to cut in early, creating an overload in the middle.

Both Cunha and Mbeumo are not typical wingers but instead prefer to move inside. Cunha in particular, if played off the left, looks like he could fit very well into a Pochettino system.

Whoever gets picked, they better get used to one thing – running. One of the cornerstones of a Pochettino team is that when they are out of possession, the team is pressing as a unit to win the ball back.

At Spurs, the front three plus the midfield three would press as one but do it smartly. One would go to the ball carrier while the others would move to mark opposition players and eliminate passing routes.

This is why Pochettino could not work with Mbappe, Neymar and Messi at PSG, for none of them were too bothered about closing down.

United players don’t have that excuse and they must be prepared for frequent, short sharp bursts of pace to close down the opposition.

This United squad is probably one of the worst in terms of player quality Pochettino has to work with in his career but his system is designed to mask over individual quality in favour of what they can do as a collective.

To make it work, he needs players to buy into his ideas, which is a problem plenty of United managers have faced in the past.

He’s had a few mistakes in recent weeks but he is still the best keeper United have.

Pochettino wants his keepers to play an active part in build up which Lammens has proven to be okay if not fantastic.

Best of a bad bunch, United would do well to strengthen here.

Pochettino likes centre backs who can pass, and Heaven fits that mould.

Similar reasoning as with Heaven. Plus Martinez will likely have a better rapport with fellow Argentine and notable man-manager Pochettino than he did with Carrick and Wilcox.

Makes the most tackles and completes the most passes per 90 of anyone in the United team, two traits Pochettino loves for his midfielders.

The picking for this position will depend on who United are facing.

If Pochettino believes United will have the majority of possession, he may go with the less mobile but more attack-focused Tielemans.

If Pochettino is expecting a tough game where United need to work hard to win the ball back, Santos would likely get the shout.

At every club he has been at, Pochettino has had good No. 10s but crucially, they have all been on the younger side.

Bruno Fernandes is 32 but still one of the league’s best players on his day. Will also be time to prove that his finger pointing to press is not just for show and he is willing to get in the trenches.

Pochettino likes his wingers to cut inside which is what Mbeumo tends to do. He looks like a player that could play in a similar mould to Son Heung Min albeit at a lesser equality.

Cunha could really shine in a Pochettino system.

At Wolves, he was nominally shown on the left of starting lineups played so centrally that he was practically a striker at times, something Pochettino has liked to do in the past.

Think prime Dele Alli or Christian Eriksen cutting in and overloading the central areas.

With Benjamin Sesko out until January, Pochettino is stuck with Zirkzee as the only recognised No. 9.

It’s not a great option to be honest but he does play like a false nine in a similar way to Kane. Which is a bit like saying a Peugeot 206 drives in a similar way to a Ferrari.

#1493. The top goalscorers for club & country in 2026 so far: Kane, Yamal, Mbappe, Raphinha…

Big names from Real Madrid, Barcelona, Arsenal and Bayern Munich feature alongside some surprise names in the most prolific goalscorers of the calendar year so far.

Some big names are surprisingly absent from the most prolific goalscorers of 2026 to date.

Drawn from Europe’s five major leagues, here are the top 10 goalscorers in 2026 across club and international competitions.

The jury is still out on Gyokeres, who remains a perplexing forward.

This calendar year has seen him look borderline anonymous and increasingly sidelined at Arsenal.

And yet Gyokeres also fired Sweden to the World Cup with a hat-trick against Ukraine and a late winner against Poland. He’s basically the Ikea Gerd Muller at this point.

Dembele has scored 20 goals in 36 PSG appearances this year, including several crucial strikes in Europe – none bigger than the equalising spot kick he coolly dispatched against Arsenal in the Champions League final.

His goal in France’s World Cup win over Iraq was, incredibly, his first in major tournament football. That was swiftly followed up with a rapid hat-trick against Norway, before another in the quarter-final against Morocco.

He is largely taking it easy right now, once again frequently rested during PSG’s domestic campaign. But he popped up with a goal against Manchester City.

Schick has had reason to celebrate in 2026. Earlier this year, he reached the milestone of 100 goals for Bayer Leverkusen.

He’s been on fire this season, with 12 goals from 14 games for the German side.

There won’t be any more international goals from Schick, though. He retired from Czech Republic duty after the World Cup.

What a year it’s been for Malen. Started it as a benchwarmer at Aston Villa. Set to finish it as one of Europe’s most lethal strikers at Roma.

Malen made an immediate impact after his January move to the Italian capital and his scoring rate has barely slowed down since.

For some reason, his form hasn’t quite translated into international football; he hasn’t scored for the Netherlands at all this year.

But high-flying Roma are laughing. Malen almost won the Serie A golden boot last season despite arriving midway through and he’s a leading contender for the gong this season.

A fairly recent entrant into the top 10 after heading into the international break on the back of a hat trick against Union Berlin.

Olise was the Bundesliga’s best assister last season but has been more than capable of finding the net himself a fair few times too.

He didn’t score any goals at the World Cup but netted the winner in Zinedine Zidane’s second game in charge of France. The best Fantasy Footballer around right now.

Yamal has long been talked up as a Ballon d’Or contender, and slowly but surely he’s getting the numbers to back it up.

The teenager’s goalscoring output has grown season on season, and 2025-26 was no exception. February’s hat-trick against Villarreal was evidence of a player about to go truly stratospheric.

Unfortunately, the final furlong of the campaign was hit by a hamstring injury, or else we suspect he’d be a few places higher up in this list.

He needed just 10 minutes in his first World Cup start to find the back of the net, although that would be his only goal in Spain’s triumph out in North America.

Now he’s looking fit and hungry – at least based on the evidence of his exceptional form of late.

The Brazilian has an exceptional tally of 33 goals for Barcelona so far this calendar year (plus one for Brazil), which is especially impressive when you consider he’s missed quite a lot of action due to injury.

He averages a goal every 49 minutes for Barca this season – to put that in context, Kylian Mbappe averages a goal every 84 minutes for Real Madrid.

Raphinha has scored in all but three of the Barca games he’s played in in 2026-27, scoring hat tricks in two, and currently leads the Europe-wide goalscoring charts with 15 in the league.

The top three are the last three winners of the European Golden Shoe. This list has taken a while to take shape, but the frontrunners are the usual suspects.

Haaland’s four goals against Iraq and Senegal in the group stages finally saw him climb up into the top 10, from which he was surprisingly absent in the latter half of the 2025-26 club season, before he added to his World Cup tally against the Ivory Coast. Then there were two goals against Brazil.

He finally drew a blank as Norway exited the World Cup at the hands of England at the quarter-final stage. He earned a well-deserved rest before spearheading Man City’s new era under Enzo Maresca.

Same as it ever was with nine goals in nine Premier League appearances for City this season, plus braces against Porto and PSG and another Champions League goal against his favourite opponents, RB Leipzig.

Like his rival Haaland, it somehow took Mbappe until mid-June to enter the top 10.

Mbappe kicked off the year in superb style, scoring in six successive starts for Real Madrid (nine goals in total) before dipping considerably with just one goal in his next seven appearances.

By the nature of his 10 goals at the World Cup, we don’t expect to see the Real Madrid superstar dropping back out. His Champions League record is pretty sensational.

Arguably the finest player in world football right now. How often have you been able to say that about an Englishman?

The only player in Europe’s five major leagues to average a better-than-goal-a-game output so far this calendar year, the England captain has 41 goals in 40 appearances for Bayern Munich in all competitions in 2026 – including home and away against Real Madrid and PSG.

He capped off his superb season with a hat-trick in the DFB Pokal final. Two goals against Croatia showed Kane carried his form into the World Cup, where he eventually scored six times.

Unbelievably, the Norway game was Kane’s first knockout appearance for club and country in 2025-26 in which he didn’t score. Which, of course, he followed with a blank against Argentina.

Surprisingly enough, Kane failed to add to his tally by drawing a blank in his first three Bayern appearances of the 2026-27 campaign.

But it’s back to normal service with his Bayern tally standing at 10 goals in 14 games. The Czechs and Croatia have been on the receiving end in the Nations League too.

Still some way to go before catching Lionel Messi’s calendar year record, mind.

#1491. Alexander Isak starts to justify £125m price tag with double

There was a centre-forward who played for Newcastle a couple of years ago. Do you remember him? He was as quick as greased lightning, played on his instincts, had a shot like cannon and could come up with a finish for every situation.

Everyone wanted him, but Liverpool signed him for £125m in August 2025. His name was Alexander Isak but shortly after arriving on Merseyside, it was like he went missing, as the guy who played in red last season bore only a physical resemblance to the guy who had played in black-and-white.

If you had wondered what had happened to him, he reappeared at Portman Road. They say good things come to those who wait. Although nobody at Liverpool would have expected such a delay to see the real Isak, there were no complaints that his career at the club has finally taken off.

Taking the headlines from Bradley Barcola on a big night at Portman Road was going to take some doing, but Isak did just that with a double salvo in the opening nine minutes, a flurry so potent it was like a boxer charging out of their corner and seeing the first blows land flush on their opponent’s jaw.

Poor Ipswich. There is universal recognition that Liverpool are a team – and a club – in transition but they had four players in Isak, Florian Wirtz, Cody Gakpo and Victor Muñoz who had the potential to dismantle the hosts if they clicked and that is precisely what happened.

“With Alex, it is clear,” said Andoni Iraola. “If he is fit, if he is available, if he is in a good shape, he will produce the numbers. My demand with Alex will not be about the goals. It will be about other things so we can play well. And if we play well, we are in good positions. Then goals will come.”

So for all the noisy backing they received from the stands and for all the effort Gary O’Neil’s side put into a contest that TV companies had chosen to broadcast because there was a potential for drama, Isak blew a hole in Ipswich’s hull in the sixth minute and they were submerging from there on in.

A blistering finish from Alexander Isak! 💥 pic.twitter.com/jSGlIZsQtA

How Isak, who had scored against Nottingham Forest last weekend, needed a night like this when he made a genuine difference. But the same was true, too, for Iraola. We live in an era where someone has to be in the eye of a storm and the Basque will know what comes with his new territory.

It had clearly irritated Iraola that Liverpool had gone behind four times in their opening two fixtures and during his pre-match media briefing, he effectively gave a sermon at one point on how slow starts, or giving the opposition a helping hand, would no longer be tolerated.

Quietly, Iraola is making his presence felt. The task he faces is significantly different than the one O’Neil is accomplishing – keeping Ipswich in the division against the odds – but Liverpool’s head coach is a man who knows his own mind and is not afraid to make decisions.

He had responded to criticism of his midfield at Newcastle on the opening weekend by dropping Ryan Gravenberch for the fixture with Forest and his response to scrutiny about his right-back seven days ago was to drop Jeremie Frimpong and bring in Ronald Araújo.

Iraola certainly picked the right team: Araújo, the loan capture from Barcelona, added stature to the back four and there was harmony in how they moved. The Uruguayan’s first instinct was to stay back and Liverpool looked better for it, even if O’Neil, incredibly, felt Ipswich had the better of things.

Emersonn, Ipswich’s Brazilian striker, did not see the ball in the opening exchanges and, by the time he did, Liverpool had zoomed into the distance to such an extent that you felt it was going to be impossible for them to peg their visitors back.

“I hate having to talk about good performances when you do not get points,” O’Neil declared to a room full of raised eyebrows and you can only assume his message was to ensure that morale in the dressing room was not drooping.

What damage was inflicted with Liverpool’s first significant attack. Gakpo, the subject of an £80m bid from Manchester City, was never going to allow transfer speculation to disrupt his focus and he nudged a perfect little ball into Isak’s path in the sixth minute to show his wellbeing.

The next move announced the return of Isak. One touch gave him an avenue to shoot, the next was a shot with his right foot that was so hard from 16 yards, on an angle, it bent the wrists of Kjell Scherpen as it howled into the net. Critics will feel Ipswich’s keeper should have done better.

Your first thought was to think of the first goal Isak scored in English football in September 2022, a similarly venomous drive, against Liverpool at Anfield. He oozed quality that evening, his pace and skill had Jürgen Klopp’s defenders persistently fretting and this is what he was doing again.

It was no coincidence that three minutes later, he came up with another wonderful goal. This one owed much to the beautiful pass Gakpo presented to him, an inch-perfect through ball with the outside of his right foot, but Isak still showed great poise to bamboozle Scherpen.

Inside NINE minutes Alexander Isak has two goals! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/3UGq0bwqRm

“He owes me a few assists now!” chirped the selfless Gakpo.

A hat-trick could have arrived in the 32nd minute but Isak was a kneecap offside as he dispatched a pass from Wirtz and, perhaps, he will have been disappointed to have made way on the hour having not secured the match ball for his efforts.

Liverpool, too, will be frustrated that they did not made sure of three points before the time Isak made way for Barcola – what Alexis Mac Alliser was thinking when he fluffed an unmarked header from six yards, only he will know – but it was not a night to nitpick.

There will be easier assignments on the horizon for Ipswich, even though O’Neil insisted they more than held their own against world-class opponents. And you can say for sure there will be more goals and wins for Liverpool and Isak if they continue in this encouraging manner.

“I witnessed what a great coach he was at Bournemouth. He is not the sort of manager you are going to see making clever patterns in his box. He just does not see the risk. He will want to get the ball to the players who want to make a difference. Coaches do not show how good they are by how they play out from the back. The important thing is when you get it in the final third, you make things happen. That is what he will want to improve. He will want Alexander Isak when he has not got the ball to press. He will want the same of Florian Wirtz. The difficulty will come with Champions League football and not putting too many demands on his players. If he gets it right, he has got a wonderful squad to work with.”

"My demands will not be about the goals, my fights with him are about other stuff." Andoni Iraola speaking about Alexander Isak 🔊 pic.twitter.com/B4zUG2IGfS

“He has had good minutes, a good pass in a counter, a good couple of chances when he was going against the goalkeeper and we have not found him. We need to learn these movements because he will be there threatening in behind all the team. But he looks confident on the ball as always. He had not played any competitive minutes since the World Cup so we had to be a little bit more careful.”

"Yeah, that's nice" 😁Alexander Isak talks through his second goal vs Ipswich 🔍 pic.twitter.com/diG2xv50Bw

“We were waiting for the first win, and we were talking about starting the game well, which we have not done recently. And we did that with two goals. With a normal pre-season, I think we are starting to get the way we want to play, being offensive and attack the defence. We showed that today. We scored two and could have scored more.

“It was not easy. It was a long injury, a difficult season [last season] in general. I was thinking; I want to have a good World Cup firstly and then to start the season well, which I feel like I have done now. That season is kind of behind me, but it was not easy.”

They absolutely love what they saw. Some of his skills, his movement. That comes from his goal last week and the confidence that brings. Fingers crossed he can carry this on.”

The Swede’s two early goals have earned Liverpool all three points at Portman Road and the travelling Liverpool fans are singing his name. Isak’s fellow teammates are pushing him towards the travelling fans to take their adulation as they belt out his name.

The final whistle goes at Portman Road and Andoni Iraola picks up his first win as Liverpool boss with a 2-0 victory thanks to Isak’s quickfire double inside the opening 10 minutes. Like they did two seasons ago, Liverpool win 2-0 at Portman Road.

Enciso has a late shot from the edge of the box but it goes wide of the far post.

McAteer shoots from range but there is not enough power to trouble Alisson, who makes the save down to his right.

A late change from Liverpool as Koumas replaces Wirtz.

Due to that VAR review for the Liverpool penalty that was not, there will probably be five or six added minutes.

Clarke’s shot from just outside the Liverpool penalty area takes a deflection off his teammate Diop and goes wide.

Davis is getting a fair bit of joy down Ipswich’s left and the ball has been on to him quite a few times. He is being afforded too much space by Liverpool to get crosses in.

Andoni Iraola is bringing on Nyoni for Mac Allister, who was on a booking.

Davis is found making a run in behind and his cross from the left side of the box is blocked by Araujo and goes behind for a corner. Lukic’s delivery is headed away at the front post by Gravenberch.

Double change for Ipswich as McAteer and Ouattara replace Fatawau and Palacios.

Barcola drives down Liverpool’s left and, as he approaches the Ipswich box, cuts onto his right and feeds it across to Gakpo, whose shot misses the target.

The ball comes to Flemming on the edge of the box and he tries to curl one into the far corner but it is an easy save for Alisson.

Barcola is nearly played in behind but Scherpen does really to get out of his goal quickly and gets to the ball first, just ahead of Barcola.

Davis and Ipswich can count themselves very, very lucky. It would have been a penalty but Szoboszlai was offside when the original ball was played. For the second time tonight, an offside call massively goes in Ipswich’s favour; one to deny Isak a hat-trick and now to deny Liverpool a penalty. A massive let-off for Ipswich.

Liverpool are demanding a penalty. Szoboszlai is played in behind and is constantly having his shirt pulled by Davis. Davis then appears to bring Szoboszlai down inside the box but the referee waves it away. Davis gets none of the ball and the referee is being sent to the screen...

Barcola’s first few touches in a Liverpool shirt are pretty good down the left. He is playing in his most natural position of wide left, with Gakpo now down the middle and Szoboszlai on the right.

Gary O’Neil is going to make a double change as Clarke and Flemming come on, with the latter making his debut. Maeda and Emersonn come off.

So, here comes from the £123m Frenchman as Barcola enters the fray for his Liverpool debut. Gravenberch also comes on. There will be no first Liverpool hat-trick for Isak as he heads off, as does Munoz.

Bradley Barcola comes on to make his Liverpool debut! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/PjO78nlcqj

Andoni Iraola must be ripping his air out with the lack of composure and control from his side since half-time. It is no wonder he is about to turn to his bench and a certain Frenchman.

Enciso is given far too much space to drive towards the Liverpool box before shooting but Alisson makes the save. Liverpool, despite being 2-0 up, have showed a real lack of composure since the break.

If trends are anything to go by, Bradley Barcola will be introduced in the next three or four minutes. Andoni Iraola likes to change things around the hour mark and if the Frenchman warms up anymore, he will nearly overheat.

Kerkez is the latest player into the book for a foul on Fatawu.

Fatawu receives it out on the right for Ipswich and cuts inside onto his preferred left foot before curling an effort towards the far post but it goes wide.

Jacquet takes a heavy touch from a high ball and ends up taking out Emersonn, which earns the Frenchman a booking.

Liverpool work it well down their left as Isak plays it into Gakpo, who drives towards the Ipswich box. He plays it across the face of the penalty area to Szboszblai, who flicks it first time into the path of Wirtz. The German’s effort takes a deflection and goes behind for a corner.

Szoboszlai’s outswinger finds a free Mac Allister at the front post but the Argentine’s header is straight at Scherpen. That was a good chance for Mac Allister.

We are back under way at Portman Road. No changes for either side at the break.

We have just seen replays of a possible penalty shout for Liverpool right at the end of the first half for a foul on Gakpo by Fatawu and it looked a decent shout.

Perhaps if Liverpool were playing a team with a bit more savvy, the 2-0 scoreline they currently protect would have been in jeopardy. Ipswich have put some nice moves together and had half chances but not enough to really turn the screw. Andoni Iraola, certainly, has been unhappy at times and it is becoming a trademark to see him spin around from the technical area in disgust when a ball has been squandered. In the main, though, he can be satisfied with this opening 45 minutes. Liverpool should be winning from here.

The first half is brought to an end at Portman Road and Isak’s quickfire double early in the half gives Liverpool a 2-0 lead at the break.

Wirtz feeds a lovely pass into the left channel to pick out the run of Isak into the Ipswich box but Diop comes in with a crucial challenge.

Two added minutes at the end of this first half.

Araujo slices a clearance out of play for an Ipswich corner. A real gift for the home side as Araujo was not under any real pressure.

Isak should head away at the near post but it comes to Mac Allister to clear away.

A chance for Wirtz as the ball falls to the German on the edge of the Ipswich box but his shot is saved by Scherpen down to his left.

Enciso is the first Ipswich player into the book tonight for delaying a restart.

Szoboszlai, for the third time in the half, shoots from range. Again, the Hungarian gets plenty of power on it but fortunately for Scherpen it is straight at him.

Enciso turns neatly not far outside the Liverpool box and then shoots but slices the shot a fair way wide.

Tommy Elphick, a member of Andoni Iraola’s coaching staff, is booked for his protestations. Liverpool are not happy with some of the fouls being given against them and then some that are not given for them, including a clear foul from Emersonn on Van Dijk that was not penalised.

Isak has the ball in the Ipswich net for the third time tonight and thinks he has his hat-trick but the offside flag goes up. It comes from a stunning piece of play from Wirtz down Liverpool’s left, taking up a pocket of space and taking the ball on the turn beautifully. He then spots Isak in space at the far post and picks him out perfectly, with Isak slotting home. However, the offside flag is up and replays prove he was just offside. Could Isak have timed his run just fractionally better and still reached the cross? Probably but it was very close.

Mac Allister receives a pass from Wirtz and, from just outside the box, decides to shoot but his effort goes just over. Scherpen did appear to have it covered anyway.

A crucial intervention from Araujo. Enciso drives down Ipswich’s right after Fatawu’s header, with Mac Allister tracking back. From the right side of the Liverpool box, Enciso’s deflected cross comes towards Maeda at the far post but Araujo makes an important clearance.

Moments later, Davis again meets a Fatawu cross at the far post but his header is off target.

Fatawu’s dangerous cross from the right all the way to the back post finds Davis, who heads back across goal. Emersonn takes a touch with his chest on the edge of the six-yard box before shooting but Jacquet is on hand to make a crucial block. Ipswich though do have their first corner of the game.

Lukic clips it in and Alisson should punch away with ease. However, the ball comes off Gakpo and, very fortunately for Alisson, the ball gets trapped between his own legs and he can gather. Alisson will be a relieved man.

Szoboszlai sends another powerful shot from range towards the goal and forces Scherpen into another decent save. Ipswich are not helping themselves at times by just giving the ball away inside their own half.

Szoboszlai comes close to adding a third for Liverpool. Fatawu inexplicably gives the ball away inside his own half before Mac Allister plays it forward to Szoboszlai, who takes just one touch before firing towards goal. Scherpen gets down well to his right to make the save.

And there he is. You have been waiting 12 months to see the Alexander Isak of Newcastle play for Liverpool but here he is, a confident, instinctive-finishing menace. His first goal was marvellous, his second was a work of art, given the pass from Cody Gakpo, and what a position Liverpool have put themselves in to get their first win under Andoni Iraola. And, while we are at it, Gakpo has made both Liverpool’s goals: what on earth were they doing thinking of selling him to Manchester City?

Isak, on his last trip to Portman Road, scored a hat-trick for Newcastle here in a 4-0 win back in December 2024. He already has two goals to his name tonight inside the opening quarter of an hour.

Emersonn misses from close range for Ipswich but the offside flag goes up against Greaves. It was a bad miss from Emersonn but Greaves, who had delivered the cross for Emersonn, was offside.

The first booking of the game goes the way of Mac Allister, who is booked slightly harshly for a foul on Enciso.

Moments later, Ipswich have their first effort of the game but Fatawu curls over from the edge of the box.

Another fine goal from Isak and Liverpool lead 2-0 not even 10 minutes into this game. It is Gakpo who assists again with a superb pass with the outside of his right foot from halfway into the left channel to pick out the run in behind of Isak. The Swede cuts inside Greaves onto his right before then chopping back onto his left. He then coolly slots home past Scherpen and Liverpool have the dream start.

Inside NINE minutes Alexander Isak has two goals! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/3UGq0bwqRm

Liverpool take a deserved lead at Portman Road. Kerkez wins the ball back for Liverpool on halfway and the ball comes to Gakpo. The Dutchman drives forward and spots Isak in space to his right. Isak’s movement is very clever as he drifts off the defender into space. He takes a touch before smashing the ball past Scherpen at his near post. Should Scherpen have saved that? Possibly but Isak did hit that very hard. For the first time this season, Liverpool lead in a Premier League match.

A blistering finish from Alexander Isak! 💥 pic.twitter.com/jSGlIZsQtA

Wirtz is penalised for a very soft foul on Enciso, who just threw his hands in the air after the slightest bits of contact. The referee Darren England was not initially going to give it but eventually does, giving Ipswich the chance to swing it in from the left into the Liverpool penalty area.

Fatawu swings it in with his left but Alisson punches away.

It has been all Liverpool in these early stages but have yet to have a shot. Ipswich have barely touched the ball thus far.

Liverpool win the first corner of the game as Davis is forced to put it behind after good work from Munoz down Liverpool’s right.

Szoboszlai’s outswinger is headed away from danger.

Both sides emerge from the tunnel at Portman Road and we are moments away from kick-off. Here is a reminder of how the two sides line up this evening:

The Paraguayan is in his second stint at Ipswich and has two assists to his name in the first two league games.

“It gives us a big belief that we can compete at the level. Coming up from the Championship, there is always some doubt around. The home win over Sunderland was huge for us. And then to be in the game for as long as we were at Manchester United was impressive. I have challenged the lads a lot. We do not focus on the outcome or results, we just commit to being the best version of ourselves. We cannot go toe-to-toe with everyone. We have to be sensible and smart.”

Andoni Iraola has made a change at right-back tonight, with Ronaldu Araujo replacing Jeremie Frimpong. Araujo arrived at Liverpool this summer on loan with an option to buy from Barcelona.

Andoni Iraola wondered what might happen when he first sat down to talk with Bradley Barcola.

Here was one of the world’s best wingers, with his 13 major honours, 28 international caps and £123m price tag – a combination that could easily lead a man to view himself through the prism of a superstar: never mind what I can do for you, what can you do for me?

Liverpool’s due diligence on Barcola had all been positive – not least from the currently injured Hugo Ekitike, who had been a vocal advocate of his compatriot’s capabilities to the recruitment team – but Iraola wanted to gauge for himself exactly what the 24-year-old was going to offer.

Ipswich were very active in the market upon their return to the Premier League, making 14 signings in total, with plenty of them involved tonight. Here is a sample of what Gary O’Neil’s side did during the window:

OUTS:George Hirst ⇢ Stoke, £6mAri Muric ⇢ Sassuolo, £6mHarry Clarke ⇢ Preston, £3m

Your Town at Portman Road! 👊 pic.twitter.com/gXrzYk7WaS

We are about to find out the two starting XIs at Portman Road. Will Bradley Barcola start for Liverpool on his debut?

The third matchday of the new Premier League season kicks off at Portman Road as newly-promoted Ipswich host Liverpool.

Andoni Iraola has drawn his first two games in charge of Liverpool, both 2-2 stalemates against Newcastle and Nottingham Forest respectively. Liverpool secured a move for forward Bradley Barcola from PSG in the final few days on the window for a fee that could rise to £123m and the Frenchman is set to make his Liverpool debut tonight.

“We are very happy with Bradley,” Iraola said. “He was our priority; to sign a very good player in that position. He has come with the right mentality. I like that he wanted Liverpool a lot, he just wanted to come here. That is a good first sign. Being the player he is and the things he has won recently, he has come with the willingness to help us. I am very happy with him.

“He trained well with us, and if everything goes well in today’s [Thursday] training, he will definitely be available for tomorrow [tonight]. He has trained with us three times. He has not had minutes in pre-season but he has been training normally with the group. It is a decision we have to make. We have to consider that he has not had minutes in pre-season.”

Liverpool won both fixtures when Ipswich were last in the Premier League two seasons ago, including a 2-0 win on the opening weekend in Arne Slot’s first game in charge of Liverpool as they went on to win the Premier League that season.

Ipswich won their first home game on their return to the Premier League, beating Sunderland 2-1 on the opening weekend. However, they fell to a 5-2 defeat in their first away game at Manchester United. Over the course of the summer transfer window, Ipswich made a total of 14 signings and spent over £200m.

“What we can do is perform in a way that always gives us a real chance, which we have done so far,” Ipswich boss Gary O’Neil said. “We were in that game at Manchester United until a couple of moments took it away from us. We were in it, so that is what we need to do, we need to make sure that no matter who it is, whether it is Liverpool, Manchester United, Manchester City, when they come to Portman Road, we need to make sure we are right in the game to give ourselves opportunities. We will always be a threat; we have scored four goals in two games. That is really good for a promoted side. We look a goal threat, and we need to keep that going and that will be tested.”

Team news from Portman Road to follow shortly.

#1490. Man Utd & Palace shocking in 2026-27 Premier League wage bill vs. position comparison

Chelsea, Tottenham Hotspur, Manchester United, Liverpool, Manchester City and Arsenal are all sitting in vastly contrasting places when you compare their wage bill rankings to their league positions after the first four games of the 2026-27 Premier League season.

Of course, it’s still early in the season. Ten matches can tell us only so much about how the season will eventually play out, and the table is still taking shape.

Still, there are already some big, eye-catching differences between wage outlay and performance.

Brighton lead the way. They are second in the Premier League despite having the 15th-highest wage bill, which stands at just £51million. That is a remarkable +13 difference between their league position and wage ranking.

Brentford are second in that regard. They are eighth while ranking 17th for wages, with a £49million annual bill, giving them a +9 difference. Hull City are fourth, sitting 13th despite having the 19th-highest wage bill at just £16million. Their +6 difference is another remarkable return for a newly-promoted side.

Leeds United have also made an impressive start. They occupy 9th place while sitting 14th in the wage rankings. Their annual wage bill is only £53million, giving them a +5 difference.

Ipswich are another side punching well above their wage bill. They sit 14th while ranking 18th for wages, with an annual wage bill of just £20million. That’s a +4 difference.

The traditional powerhouses have produced a mixed bag. Arsenal are top while having the third-highest wage bill in the division, at £154million. That puts them two places ahead of their wage position, while Manchester City sit third in the league and second in the wage rankings.

Chelsea are fifth with the seventh-highest wage bill, £97million, while top spenders Liverpool are fourth. The Reds have the highest wage bill in the Premier League at £177million but sit three places below that ranking.

The other ‘Big Six’ underachievers are not hard to spot. Manchester United are 18th with the fourth-highest wage bill of £152million, while Tottenham are 11th despite having the fifth-highest at £138million. Oof.

Villa are also slightly off the pace. They are 10th despite having the sixth-highest wage bill, with £98million going on salaries. That puts them four places below their wage ranking.

We’ve ranked every Premier League club by the gap between their league position and wage-bill ranking, from the biggest overperformers to the biggest underperformers. Keep an eye on this one, as we’ll be keeping it updated as the season progresses.

#1488. Much-improved Newcastle stop the rot with a 1-1 draw at Fulham - but 'slapstick' defending and wasteful finishing will leave Matthias Jaissle rueing a missed opportunity, writes CRAIG HOPE

Published: 12:52 EST, 7 November 2026 | Updated: 19:24 EST, 7 November 2026

Just when Newcastle looked set for victory after Jacob Murphy had borrowed Amar Dedic's bow to arrow them into a late lead, they turned the weapon on themselves.

After a week in which Dedic, Bosnia's answer to Robin Hood, had made headlines when pursued by police for wandering around the Northumberland countryside with his hunting gear, the Geordies were ready to rob the good folk of west London after Murphy found the target ten minutes from time.

Less than three minutes later and they were picking the arrow from their own foot. William Osula failed to protect possession and allowed Fulham to enter the penalty area. Then, with the ball bouncing around the goalmouth, it was home substitute Rodrigo Muniz who pounced to punish Newcastle's scruffy defending.

'Slapstick', visiting boss Matthias Jaissle later called it.

The German also said that his team deserved to win but you got the impression he was relieved to emerge without defeat, especially as the performance was improved on the back of a run of four losses in five.

Newcastle's second-half spirit also showed a response to a week of noise centred on dressing-room unrest, not to mention Dedic's police drama.

Jacob Murphy thought he had won it for Newcastle after scoring late on at Craven Cottage

Rodrigo Muniz netted moments later after sloppy defending from Newcastle, earning a 1-1 draw

Matthias Jaissle's side were much improved but must cut out the errors to win matches

And Jaissle was right in that his team could have left with three points had master archer Harvey Barnes not missed a hat-trick of chances.

Fulham (4-2-3-1): Leno 7; Castagne 6 (Tete 77, 5), Affengruber 6, Bassey 6, Robinson 5; Berge 6, Charles 6; Bobb 6 (Sessegnon 78, 6), King 7 (Palacios 72, 5), Iwobi 6; Garcia 4 (Muniz 65, 8)

Subs not used: Lecomte, Andersen, Hugo Larsson, Manuel Angel, Kevin

Newcastle (4-2-3-1): Hornicek 7; Dedic 6, Thiaw 7 (Schar 85, 6), Burn 7, Hall 6; Nico Gonzalez 5 (Miley 61, 6), Steur 7 (Fernandez-Pardo 74, 5); Murphy 8, Wissa 6 (Willock 61, 5), Barnes 6; Osula 5 (Elanga 85)

Subs not used: Pope, Livramento, Botman, Bazoumana Toure

The winger is the player to whom they'd want those opportunities to fall, too. But twice before half-time, when denied by Bernd Leno from close range, and then again when lashing wide after the break, he failed to give his side the advantage.

Murphy corrected his team-mate's finishing when capitalising on a loose pass from Cesar Palacios and slamming into the bottom corner from 25 yards, but that joy was short-lived.

In truth, there hadn't been much joy to behold all afternoon. The draw keeps both sides in the bottom half of the table, and that is where they will likely stay.

The first half, in particular, had very strong last-on-Match-of-the-Day vibes.

Newcastle thought they had a 33rd-minute lead when Dan Burn stole in at the near post to flick home from Murphy's low cross.

What the officials had spotted at the far post was linebacker Yoane Wissa pinning defender Timothy Castagne, and so playing Burn onside. It was the right call, even if Jaissle disagreed

'I learned that word here, a 'soft' decision. In my eyes, it was not right,' he said. 'But I was pleased with our complete commitment and togetherness.

'We grew through the game and that was excellent, something to build on. We showed the fundamentals.'

Dedic twice came close to creating goals with teasing crosses from the right, and you wondered if he would have mimicked Barnes' trademark archer celebration had they been converted.

He was kept away from the media post-match, but Jaissle did say: 'He played well, right? It (the bow & arrow incident) didn't affect him. He was not aware of the rules. We don't need to make a big deal out of it.'

Fulham's Josh King was included in Thomas Tuchel's England squad on Friday, the club's first Three Lions call-up in eight years. He, however, now needs a scan on a tight groin before learning if he's fit enough to feature.

Did the 19-year-old play like a would-be England international? He was his side's best player in the first half, even if that was a low bar to hurdle. One volley would have raised the roof had it gone in, so sweet was the connection from 20 yards. Lukas Hornicek needed every inch of his 6ft 6in frame to dive and save. And that, too, was a recurring theme, Newcastle's reliance on the big Czech to bail them out when giving up chances.

Like Newcastle, however, Fulham simply weren't good enough to take them.

#1486. In vivo CAR-T double knockout screen maps synergistic antitumour gene pairs

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Nature (2026) Cite this article

Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-T cell therapy has transformed the treatment of haematological malignancies, but its efficacy remains limited by multiple negative regulatory mechanisms intrinsic to T cells1,2,3,4. Here we perform a high-throughput in vivo CAR-T double-knockout (DKO) CRISPR screen, and identify multiple DKO gene pairs that are both effective and synergistic. The top pair, NR4A1–SOCS3 DKO, has multiple favourable immunological features. Whole-transcriptome profiling and in vivo single-cell RNA sequencing reveal that NR4A1–SOCS3 DKO specifically upregulates metabolic pathways in CAR-T cells, which show significantly higher metabolic fitness and mitochondrial activity. NR4A1–SOCS3 DKO CAR-T cells and T cells exhibit exceptionally potent antitumour efficacy and long-term tumour control across different tumour models without compromising safety features. NR4A1–SOCS3 DKO outperforms several benchmark single-gene and dual-gene modifications in T cells and CAR-T cells5,6,7,8,9. These data demonstrate high-throughput in vivo CAR-T DKO screening for rapid discovery of combination targets, and establish NR4A1–SOCS3 as a promising pair of intracellular checkpoints to engineer high-performance CAR-T therapies against cancer.

a, Quantification of CD3− cells 5 days after CRISPR-mediated gene editing in three independent donors. b, Quantification of live cells 5 days after editing with the indicated Cas9 mRNA concentrations, n = 3 biologically independent replicates. Data are shown as mean + s.e.m. Significance was calculated using one-way ANOVA with Dunnett’s multiple-comparisons test. ns, not significant. c, Left, representative flow cytometry plots showing CD3 and CD28 protein-level DKO efficiency in activated human primary T cells 5 days after Cas9 mRNA electroporation. Right, quantification of CD3+ CD28+ cells in DKO and vector control groups; data are shown as mean + s.e.m.; n = 4 infection replicates. Significance was calculated using a paired two-sided t-test, ****P < 0.0001. d, Quantification of CD3− or CD28− cells 5 days after editing; n = 3 donors per concentration. Data are shown as mean ± s.e.m. e, Classification and composition of targeted genes in the T cell DKO CRISPR library. f, Schematic of the two-step T cell DKO CRISPR library construction process. g, Quantification of plasmid library sgRNA-pair construct distribution. h, Flow cytometry histograms showing EGFRvIII expression in U87-GL and U87-GL-EGFRvIII cell lines. i, Flow cytometry histograms showing PD-L1 expression in U87-GL and U87-GL-EGFRvIII cell lines. j, Schematic of DKO CAR-T cell library generation pipeline, including human T cell isolation and activation, CAR-T cell generation and selection, lentiviral DKO CRISPR library infection and Cas9 mRNA electroporation. Schematic in panel j created in BioRender; Chen, S. https://biorender.com/4g9xapi (2026). k, Spider plots of tumour volumes for donor 1 in vivo screen experiment shown in Fig. 1d. n = 5 biologically independent mice. l, Representative H&E-stained tumour sections from two biologically independent tumours per group from the screen shown in Fig. 1c. Scale bar, 250 μm. m, sgRNA-pair detection rates from the total library across individual samples. D, donor; T, tumour. n, Heat map of Spearman correlation coefficients between the log2-normalized counts-per-million (log-norm.) sgRNA counts for each sample. Data were arranged by hierarchical clustering using the ward.D2 method. o, Multidimensional scaling analysis of log2-normalized screen data using the top 10,000 most variable sgRNA pairs across samples. Data points were clustered by k-means. p, Box-dot plot of library representation across individual samples, showing the distribution of all sgRNA-pair constructs counts. Boxes indicate the 25th–75th percentiles, center lines indicate medians, and whiskers extend to the most extreme values within 1.5 times the interquartile range. Individual points represent sgRNA-pair counts. q, Empirical cumulative distribution function of DKO library representation among detected sgRNA pairs in plasmid, pre-injection cell and tumour samples. Sample labels in m-p indicate sample type, plasmid, pre-injection cell or tumour, and donor ID.

a, Distribution of the top four performing sgRNA-pair constructs for top DKO hits across samples, ranked by SAMBA sgRNA z-score. b, Heat map of DKO screen scores for all pairwise gene combinations assessed in the CRISPR screen. Values were scaled and visualized within a range of −1 to 1. Hierarchical clustering was performed using the Ward.D2 method based on Euclidean distances. c, Scatter plot showing the relationship between screen enrichment and synergistic effect. SAMBA z-scores were plotted against synergy scores for each gene pair. Dashed lines indicate FDR-adjusted P value, q < 0.05, for epistasis and SAMBA results. d, Scatter plot of observed DKO SAMBA scores versus expected SAMBA scores based on the additive effects of the corresponding SKOs for each gene pair (SKO1 + SKO2). Points are colored by synergy score. Linear regression yielded R2 = 0.0152 (n = 2,485 gene pairs; 71 SKO genes), indicating minimal predictability of DKO outcomes from SKO additivity. e, Quantification of indel frequencies in DKO-edited CAR-T cells 5 days after electroporation across three independent batches. P values were calculated using unpaired two-sided t-tests. Data are mean ± s.e.m.; n = 3 human donors. Each dot represents one human donor. f, Quantification of indel frequencies in CAR-T cells from three donors generated across three independent batches 90 days after gene editing. P values were calculated using one-way ANOVA with Dunnett’s multiple-comparisons test versus GTC. Data are mean + s.e.m.; n = 3 independent donor-derived CAR-T cell preparations, generated from three donors in independent batches. NS, not significant, *P < 0.05, **P < 0.01, ***P < 0.001, ****P < 0.0001.

a, Quantification of live cells 5 days after editing in different DKO CAR-T cells compared with controls, n = 3 infection replicates per group. b, Schematic of generation of DKO CAR-T or CAR-Jurkat cell generation and downstream assays. Schematic in panel b created in BioRender; Chen, S. https://biorender.com/7vyyd1r (2026). c, Quantification of Ca2+ flux AUC and peak signal change in different DKO CAR-Jurkat samples. The resting region was defined as 1 min before antigen crosslinking, and the peak region was defined as 500 s after cross-linking. AUC is calculated as (mean peak signal – mean resting signal) × 500. Representative of three independent experiments. d, Quantification of pERK1/2 (pT202/pY204) signal in DKO CAR-Jurkat cells after U87-GL-EGFRvIII stimulation at the indicated time points; n = 3 per group per time point. e, Quantification of pERK1/2+ (pT202/pY204) DKO CAR-T cells after U87-GL-EGFRvIII cell stimulation for 30 min; n = 3 biological replicates per group. f-g, NF-κB CFP and NFAT/AP-1 GFP reporter activity after coculture of U87-GL-EGFRvIII cells with different DKO CD8+ CAR-Jurkat cells with GTC control at indicated time points. E:T = 1:2. n = 3 per group per time point. f, Schematic of the NFAT/AP-1 GFP reporter structure and quantification of GFP+ cells. g, Schematic of the NF-κB CFP reporter structure and the quantification of CFP+ cells. h, Quantifications of tonic signaling in CAR-Jurkat cells after 1 month cell culture without stimulation, n = 3. P value was determined by one-way ANOVA with Dunnett’s correction for multiple comparisons test versus GTC. i, Left, representative flow cytometry histograms showing CD107a expression in CD8+ DKO and GTC CAR-T cells after 2-h coculture with U87-GL-EGFRvIII cells. Right, quantification of CD107a+ CAR-T cells; n = 4 per group; E:T = 1:2. j, Quantification of IFN-γ, TNF, and granzyme B expression in CD8+ and CD4+ CAR-T cells after 4-h coculture with U87-GL-EGFRvIII cells at E:T = 1:8; n = 4 per group. k, Left, quantification of CellTrace Violetlow CAR-T cells after two rounds of repeated antigen stimulation, measured on day 5, n = 6 each. Right, quantification of absolute CAR-T cell numbers; n = 3 on day 0, n = 6 on day 2, 5, and 7 per group. l, Quantification of CellTrace Violetlow CAR-T cells in low IL-2 medium, measured on day 7; n = 3 per group. m, Quantification of live cells percentage in culture or after repeated challenge. n, Left, quantification of CD45RO+ CD62L+ DKO CAR-T cells after two rounds of tumour stimulation on day 5. Right, quantification of CD27+ DKO CAR-T cells after two rounds of tumour stimulation on day 5; n = 6 per group. For each round of coculture, E:T = 1:4. o, Quantifications of LAG-3, PD-1, and TIM-3 expression in CAR-T cells after repeated tumour challenge on day 5, n = 4 per group. For each round of coculture, E:T = 1:4. p, Quantification of LAG-3+, PD-1+, TIM-3+ CAR-T cells after two rounds of tumour stimulation on day 5; n = 4 per group. For each round of coculture, E:T = 1:4. q, SPICE analysis of LAG-3, PD-1, and TIM-3 expression in CAR-T cells on day 5. Data are group means. r, Quantification of absolute CAR-T cell number after IL-2 withdrawal; n = 3 per group at day 0, n = 4 per group at day 2, 5, and 7. Data in d-g,k right,m,r are mean ± s.e.m.; data in a,h-j,k left,l,n-p are mean + s.e.m. Significance levels were calculated using ordinary two-way ANOVA with Dunnett’s multiple-comparisons test comparing each group with GTC within each row or time point (d-g,j,k right,m,r), repeated-measures one-way ANOVA with Dunnett’s multiple-comparisons test versus GTC (a), or ordinary one-way ANOVA with Dunnett’s multiple-comparisons test versus GTC (h,i,k left,l,n-p). Dashed lines in c, i, j, n-p indicate mean values of the GTC group. n indicates biologically independent samples unless otherwise stated. Exact P values and detailed statistics are provided in the Source Data. Data are representative of three independent experiments using cells from human donors independent of those used in the screen. NS, not significant, *P < 0.05, **P < 0.01, ***P < 0.001, ****P < 0.0001.

a, Schematic of the time-series RNA-seq experiment in DKO, NR4A1 SKO, SOCS3 SKO, and GTC CAR-T cells undergoing repeated tumour challenges. b, Principal components analysis (PCA) of all RNA-seq samples across all stimulation time-points (left) or separated by timepoint (right). The first two principal components are shown. Genotypes are indicated by dot color, and samples are grouped by time point (left) or genotype (right) using convex hulls. c, Volcano plots of differential expression (DE) analysis for epistasis at each time-point. Significant epistatic transcripts were defined by an FDR-adjusted P value (q value) <0.05 and an absolute log2 fold change (LFC) > 0.5 for the DKO interaction term in the statistical model (Methods). Top DE transcripts are labeled based on significance and LFC, with selected transcripts shown in bold. d, Heatmaps and pathway analysis of DE transcripts from pairwise comparisons between genotypes across stimulation times. For each time point, DE transcripts were hierarchically clustered and shown as heatmaps (left). Pathway analyses were performed independently for each transcript cluster using over-representation analysis (ORA) tests with MSIGDB v7.4 Hallmark gene-sets. Significant pathways (q < 0.05; up to four pathways per cluster shown) are shown on the right, color-coded by the transcript clusters. Dot-size indicates the percentage of pathway genes that were significantly differentially expressed. e, Heatmaps of DE transcripts significantly enriched as NF-κB and STAT5B targets by transcription factor (TF) over-representation analysis (ORA). TF analysis was performed using MSIGDB v7.4 TF gene-sets; ontology names are shown above the heatmaps. f-g, Representative flow cytometry histogram and quantification of p-STAT3 and p-STAT5 in CAR-T cell groups. n = 4 (f), and n = 3 (g) biological replicates per group. h, Representative flow cytometry histograms and quantification of BAX expression in CAR-T cells. n = 3 biological replicates per group. Data in f-h are mean + s.e.m. Significance levels in f-h were calculated using one-way ANOVA with Dunnett’s multiple-comparisons versus GTC (f-g) or DKO (h). Exact P values and detailed statistics are provided in the Source Data. NS, not significant, *P < 0.05, **P < 0.01, ***P < 0.001, ****P < 0.0001.

a, Schematic of the single-cell transcriptomics (SCT) data processing pipeline. b, UMAP projections showing the T cell filtering step in the SCT analysis. B cells were identified by CD20 expression, and T cells were identified by CD3E expression. c, Dot plot showing gene signatures used for immune subset classification. Cells were classified into major immune cell categories, CD8+ T cell subsets and phenotypic states. Dot color and size indicate average gene signature z-score and percentage of expressing cells. Gene-sets used for each gene signature of the dot plot are shown in the right panel tables. d, Dot plot showing transcriptional patterns of marker genes used to classify in vivo CAR-T cell subsets in the SCT data. #1485. Newcastle’s 1995-96 squad: Name every player used that season

Newcastle United‘s 1995-96 team were nicknamed The Great Entertainers and captured the hearts of neutrals everywhere. But can you name every member of that squad?

Managed by Kevin Keegan, Newcastle played some brilliant attacking football and were 12 points clear at the top of the Premier League by January.

But Manchester United remorselessly reeled them in and Newcastle’s loss of form in the final months eventually saw them settle for second place.

We’re asking you to name everybody who played for the club that season, including the cup competitions.

There are 25 names to get and we’ve ordered them by number of appearances. We’ve also given you their positions too.

If this puts you in the mood for another quiz, why not try name every player to score 10+ Premier League goals for Newcastle?

If you enjoy our quizzes, head to our new Football Games home where you can search an archive of over 1,000 quizzes and play them all in beautiful full-screen mode.

Good luck, and don’t forget to tweet us your scores at @planetfutebol.
